## [NL-20] checks: kernel — registry with one shell per rule group, `CheckPolicy` (quote span ≥ 3, name scan blocking in `cfu_item` only, reviewer quote ≤ 12), Submit/Approve gates, structural rules (schema, sections, minutes, ELD callouts, CFU keys, heading order, table headers)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-16 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need the issue list to refresh after each save, so that I know at once if an edit broke a rule, such as deleting the only question that checks a standard. This ticket is the kernel every rule plugs into: one registry with a stub for each of the 28 check kinds, the policy numbers SP-3 set, the pure Submit and Approve gates, and the structural rules, so the later rule tickets (NL-39, 40, 41) each fill their own files and edit nothing shared (Metz C1).

### What to build
`packages/core/src/checks/` (A6a; pure; `compromise` is allow-listed for NL-40 only).
**`types.ts`.** `CheckFinding`, `CheckResult`, `CheckRule`, `CheckContext`, `GateState`, `GateIssue`, `CheckRuleList` (DO-4 §8). Heavy members of `CheckContext` (`standards`, `linked_lessons`, `pending_suggestions`, `safety_flags`, `confirmations`, `links`) and the recorded-resolution input of `merge_resolutions` are typed with narrow **structural** shapes that the richer DO-4 records satisfy (`StandardRow`, `DerivedRow`, `SuggestionRow`, `SafetyFlagRow`, `AlignmentLinkRow`, `IssueRow`, `LessonLinkRecord` arrive in NL-12/NL-38 a wave later); `lesson: StoredLesson`, `row: NormalizedRow` come from `@ls/schema`.
**`policy.ts`.** `CheckPolicy`, frozen `CHECK_POLICY` with the SP-3 values: `quote_span_min_words 3`, `reviewer_quote_max_words 12`, `quote_and_page_scans "blocking_everywhere"`, `name_scan_scope "blocking_in_cfu_items"`, `name_scan_engine "heuristic_plus_compromise"`, `minutes_target 50`, `minutes_tolerance 5`, `vocabulary_cap 6`, `safety_run_min_words 6`.
**`registry.ts`.** `CHECK_RULES`: exactly one rule per `CheckKind` (28), in `CheckKind` order (DO-4 §2). Rule files live at `rules/<group>/<kind>.ts`; each group's `index.ts` exports its `RULES`. **This ticket writes all 28 files**: the bodies of the four structural kinds, and stubs (`run` returns `[]`, `level` set) for the rest, so no later ticket edits `registry.ts`. Group map (decided here): `structural` — `schema_invalid`, `section_missing`, `minutes_out_of_range`, `vocabulary_word_missing` (blocking, PRD R-19 as amended, U2; DO-4 §13 R-8); `alignment` (NL-39) — `standard_not_taught`, `standard_not_checked`, `code_not_allowed`, `eld_label_mismatch`, `standard_confirmation`, `standard_add_suggestion`, `judge_no`; `safety` (NL-39) — `safety_flag_open`, `safety_note_without_tip`, `safety_text_in_student_block`, `disclosure_prompt`; `links` (NL-39) — `cross_lesson_link`, `linked_text_changed`, `suggestion_pending`; `grounding` (NL-40) — `quote_placeholder_open`, `excerpt_slot_open`, `quote_unmatched`, `page_out_of_range`, `proper_noun_unsourced`, `quote_without_source`, `quote_too_long`, `rights_to_clear`; `arc` (NL-41) — `arc_repeat`, `vocabulary_over_cap`. `rules/alignment/derive.ts` is a stub `derive_alignment(ctx): AlignmentLinkRow[]` returning `[]` (NL-39 fills it). `run_checks(ctx, rules, policy): CheckResult` runs every rule, orders findings by `CheckKind` order then `address`, counts `blocking` / `confirmation` / `advisory` by level, sets `first_failing_kind` to the first kind (in `CheckKind` order) with a blocking finding, and never swallows a rule's exception. Levels for the filled rules follow CON-13 and PRD R-19 as amended (§5.4): `standard_confirmation` is `confirmation`; `eld_label_mismatch`, `arc_repeat`, `vocabulary_over_cap`, `judge_no` are `advisory`; the rest (including `vocabulary_word_missing`) `blocking`; stubs take the level their owning ticket will confirm.
**`gates.ts`.** `merge_resolutions(findings, recorded): GateIssue[]` (resolved when a recorded resolution has the same `(kind, address, code)` and the kind is resolvable; resolutions never carry to a finding of another key; non-resolvable kinds: `suggestion_pending`, `standard_confirmation`, `safety_flag_open`, `safety_note_without_tip`, `safety_text_in_student_block`, `rights_to_clear`, `cross_lesson_link`: CON-13). `submit_gate(state)` → `GateDecision` with `refusals` in order `SUGGESTION_PENDING`, `BLOCKED` (unresolved blocking issues; `details.issues` lists blocking **and** confirmation), `CONFIRMATION_OPEN`; `approve_gate(state)` → `FOUR_EYES` (when enabled and `last_editor_id == approver_id`), `SUGGESTION_PENDING`, `BLOCKED`, `CONFIRMATION_OPEN`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAPPROVED` (`details` names the source lesson). `allowed` is true only with no refusal.
**Structural rules (bodies).** `schema_invalid`: heading levels never skip (an h2 followed by h4), every table has a header row, every CFU item has exactly one option marked Correct and a rationale for each option (R-58, R-15). `section_missing`: a template section absent, or a section lacking a `required_role` (including the three Integrated ELD callouts in Literacy Lab and Learning in Action, R-14). `minutes_out_of_range`: a section's `minutes` differs from the template's by more than `minutes_tolerance`, or the lesson total is outside 50 ± 5. `vocabulary_word_missing`: a word of `ctx.row.vocabulary` found in neither of the lesson's two vocabulary lists (U2: "Addressed in Lesson" = `front_matter.vocabulary`, and the "for Additional Practice" list in the `personal_dictionary` section), compared case-insensitively after trimming; one finding per missing word at the front-matter address. Addresses on findings are section addresses or `<section>.Part<X>`.
Must not: fill a non-structural rule body (NL-39/40/41), edit another ticket's rule file after this merge, read a clock or the network, or import a driver.

## [NL-21] review: lesson state machine `decide_transition` (roles, states, UXP-1/3/4/10)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-24 — As a reviewer (P-1) I need Submit to freeze the lesson, so that the approver reads exactly what I sent. US-25 — As an approver (P-3) I need to approve one pinned version. US-28 — reopening asks for a reason and makes a new version. This ticket is the one rule table for those moves, shared by the web app (most moves) and the collaboration server (Submit, the editable-state guard).

### What to build
`packages/core/src/lifecycle/lesson-machine.ts` (A12a; pure; depends on `@ls/schema`).
**`decide_transition(i: TransitionInput): TransitionDecision`** (DO-4 §8) applying CON-18's order **role → state → missing input**: `ROLE_FORBIDDEN`, then `INVALID_TRANSITION`, then `NOTE_REQUIRED` / `REASON_REQUIRED` / `RATING_REQUIRED` (a blank or whitespace-only text counts as missing). The pin, four-eyes, blocking and dependency conditions are the services' (they need data), so this function never returns them. Moves:
| action | role | from | to | `writes_snapshot` | `collab_mode_after` | missing input |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start_review` | reviewer | `draft` | `in_review` | none | none | — |
| `submit` | reviewer | `in_review`, `changes_requested`, `reopened` | `submitted` | `submit` | `read_only` | — |
| `withdraw` | reviewer | `submitted` | `in_review` | none | `editable` | none (UXP-10: no reason) |
| `approve` | approver | `submitted` | `approved` | `approve` | none (already frozen) | `rating` → `RATING_REQUIRED` |
| `request_changes` | approver | `submitted` | `changes_requested` | none | `editable` | `note` → `NOTE_REQUIRED` (the `tag` is validated by the schema, not here) |
| `reopen` | approver | `approved`, `exported` | `reopened` | `reopen` | `editable` | `reason` → `REASON_REQUIRED` (UXP-4) |
A refusal returns `{allowed: false, to_state: null, refusal: <code>, writes_snapshot: null, collab_mode_after: null}`. A second approver approving an `approved` lesson, and `start_review` on an `in_review` lesson, are `INVALID_TRANSITION` (CON-18). No path leads to `generation_failed` or `exported` (the worker and CON-23 own those).
**`transition_roles(action): RoleName[]`** gives the roles allowed to ask, checked before the lesson is loaded so `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` precedes `NOT_FOUND`. **`is_editable(state, role): boolean`** is true only for the reviewer role in `in_review`, `changes_requested` and `reopened` (CON-12 write permission: authors and approvers never edit); `WriteGuard` and `apply_edit` both call it, so a new state is one edit here.
Must not: read a repository, clock or session, return the pin, four-eyes, blocking or dependency codes, or hold an editable-state list anywhere else.

### Sources
- DO-3 §2.1 (`lesson-machine.ts`), §5 (state machine as a pure function: **cut**; editable-state list only here: Metz C3); DO-4 §8 (lifecycle: `TransitionAction`, `TransitionInput`, `TransitionDecision`, `decide_transition`, `transition_roles`, `is_editable`), §10.1 (producers), `docs/design/spec-dry-run.md` Part 2 (T2: the missing-input codes are decided here, G-11)
- CON-18 (moves, permissions, error precedence), INTERFACE *Lesson states and the moves* and shared guarantee 11; CON-12 (`write_permission`); UXP-1, UXP-3, UXP-4, UXP-6, UXP-10; PRD R-33 as amended, R-54, GR-6; WP-1 (the submit/approve path)
- **Brief check:** serves "Lesson Content Generation and Editing/Approval Workflow"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria

## [NL-22] generation: pipeline state, `route_after_checks`, circuit breaker (pure)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-8 — As an outline author (P-2) I need failed lessons to say why they failed and to be retried on their own, and a run to stop cleanly at its cap or after repeated failures, so that a few failures leave the rest of the unit reviewable and nothing is billed twice. This ticket is the pure decision layer: what the worker does next, which reason a failed tile shows, and when a run pauses, kept apart from every model call and database write (rule `agent-architecture`: code decides what next and done).

### What to build
`packages/core/src/pipeline/` (A9; pure; `@ls/schema` only).
**`state.ts`.** `LessonJobState` as in DO-4 §6 (job reference with `unit_id`, `context`, `draft_call`, `call_ids`, `draft`, `schema_issues`, `compiled`, `compile_error`, `check_result`, `repair_rounds`, `truncation_retries`, `rate_limit_retries`, `brakes_fired`, `started_at`, `cost_usd`, `outcome`) with the heavy members as **type parameters** (`LessonJobState<Ctx, Compiled, Checked>`, default `unknown`), because `ClaimedJob`, `RowContext`, `CompiledLesson` and `CheckResult` come from NL-12, NL-18 and NL-20, which are not this ticket's blockers; NL-29 instantiates it. Pure helpers: `initial_state(job, now)`, `with_brake(state, brake)` (idempotent, immutable), `wall_clock_exceeded(state, now, limit_ms)` (true only when strictly over). `BrakeName`, `NextStep`, `RouteInput`, `FailureInput`, `FailureReasonRecord` as in DO-4 §2 and §6; `ProviderErrorKind` is declared here as a literal union identical to DO-4 §10.2's (NL-12's `ProviderError.kind` uses the same union; NL-29 asserts the two are mutually assignable).
**`route-after-checks.ts`: `route_after_checks(i: RouteInput): NextStep`.** First matching row wins: `schema_valid and compiled and check_passed` → `store`; `repair_rounds < max_repair_rounds` (any failure: invalid schema, `CompileError` or a blocking finding) → `repair`; otherwise `fail`. `max_repair_rounds` is 1 (R-19), so there is never a second repair.
**`failure-reasons.ts`: `failure_reasons_for(i: FailureInput): FailureReasonRecord[]`.** One reason per row that applies, in this order: brake `cancelled` → `cancelled`; brake `spend_run_cap` / `spend_day_cap` / `spend_project_cap` → `capped`; brake `job_wall_clock` → `timeout`; brake `truncation_retry` (truncated twice) → `truncated`; provider error `rate_limited` or `overloaded` after the retries (brake `rate_limit_retries`) → `rate_limited`; provider error `timeout` → `timeout`; any other provider error → `provider_error`; `compile_error` set → `compile_error`; `schema_valid` false → `schema_invalid`; `first_failing_kind` set → `check_failed` with `check_kind`. `circuit_breaker` adds no reason. `check` values are the OpenAPI `FailureReason.check` enum exactly. `message` comes from a fixed table of plain-English strings (`FAILURE_MESSAGES`), never from model output.
**`circuit-breaker.ts`: `should_pause_run(recent: Sequence[TerminalJobView], threshold): PauseDecision`.** Considers only `ready` and `generation_failed` jobs (a `cancelled` one is ignored), takes the `threshold` most recent by `finished_at` (ties by `lesson_id`), and pauses iff all of them are `generation_failed` with the same non-null `first_failing_kind`; returns `{pause, check, lesson_ids}` (`CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SAME_CHECK` is 3).
Must not: read a clock (times are passed in), call a model, repository or queue, or format a message from untrusted text.

### Sources
- DO-3 §2.1 (`route-after-checks.ts`, `failure-reasons.ts`, `circuit-breaker.ts`), §7 (`CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SAME_CHECK`, `JOB_WALL_CLOCK_MS`); DO-4 §6 (`LessonJobState`, `RouteInput`, `route_after_checks`, `FailureInput`, `failure_reasons_for`, `FailureReasonRecord`), §8 (`TerminalJobView`, `PauseDecision`, `should_pause_run`), §2 (`BrakeName`, `FailureCheck`), §10.2 (`ProviderErrorKind`)
- CON-6 (`FailureReason`, tile states, pause rule), CON-7; OpenAPI `FailureReason`; HP-1, HP-7 (brakes, circuit breaker); PRD R-16, R-19; `docs/design/spec-dry-run.md` T3 (the decision-table gaps G-20, G-22 this ticket implements); WP-1 (a 3-minute Look Back repaired once)
- **Brief check:** serves "Lesson Content Generation and Editing/Approval Workflow"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] `route_after_checks` over every combination of `schema_valid`, `compiled`, `check_passed` (8) and `repair_rounds` 0 or 1 with `max_repair_rounds 1` (16 rows) equals the DO-4 decision table: all three true → `store`; otherwise `repair` at round 0 and `fail` at round 1 — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/route-after-checks.test.ts::table` (16 rows) — evidence: 16 passing rows — covers: R-19
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] WP-1's path: the first pass fails `minutes_out_of_range` (3-minute Look Back) → `repair`; after the one repair it passes → `store`; had it still failed → `fail` and never a second `repair` — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/route-after-checks.test.ts::wp1_one_repair` — evidence: 3 passing steps — covers: R-19, R-16
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] `failure_reasons_for` returns the reason for each row of the table (brake `cancelled` → `cancelled`, the three spend brakes → `capped`, `job_wall_clock` → `timeout`, `truncation_retry` → `truncated`, provider `rate_limited` and `overloaded` → `rate_limited`, provider `timeout` → `timeout`, `auth` → `provider_error`, compile error → `compile_error`, invalid schema → `schema_invalid`, failing kind → `check_failed` with `check_kind`), and combinations keep the table's order (e.g. `spend_run_cap` + invalid schema → `[capped, schema_invalid]`) — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/failure-reasons.test.ts` (14 single rows + 3 combinations) — evidence: 17 passing cases; every `check` value is in the OpenAPI enum — covers: M-15, R-16
- [ ] AC-4 [negative] reason messages are fixed strings: no message contains a brace, a model output, a prompt or a lesson text (a planted marker `RAW-MODEL-TEXT-2f9` passed as `compile_error` appears nowhere in the returned messages), `check_kind` is set only for `check_failed`, and `circuit_breaker` adds no reason — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/failure-reasons.test.ts::messages_fixed` — evidence: passing; marker count 0 — covers: M-44
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] `should_pause_run` with threshold 3: three newest terminal jobs failing the same kind → `pause true`, `check` that kind, `lesson_ids` in order; two same plus one different → no pause; a `ready` job among the three resets; `cancelled` jobs are ignored; fewer than 3 jobs → no pause; ties on `finished_at` break by `lesson_id`; threshold 2 works — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/circuit-breaker.test.ts` (8 cases) — evidence: 8 passing cases — covers: M-44
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] `with_brake` is idempotent and immutable (the input state is unchanged, a second call with the same brake adds nothing); `wall_clock_exceeded` is false at exactly the limit and true one millisecond over; `initial_state` sets `started_at` to the passed time and all counters to 0 — verify: `npm test -- packages/core/src/pipeline/state.test.ts` — evidence: 5 passing cases — covers: M-44

- [ ] AC-8 [regression/context] area map A9 rows for `packages/core/src/pipeline/**` planned → actual; the type-parameter choice for `LessonJobState` noted for NL-29 in the dev log; dev-log entry — verify: `git diff --stat` and `python3 ~/.claude/skills/icm-project/scripts/check_context.py .` — evidence: diff touches only those rows; no FAIL

Acceptance anchor: WP-1 (`docs/data/worked-pairs.md`, the draft with a 3-minute Look Back repaired once) is one of this ticket's tests (AC-2).

### Observability
N/A — pure functions: no entry point, record or log line. WF-22 (the lesson job, NL-29/NL-79) calls them and stores `brakes_fired`, `failure_reasons_json` and the pause on the job and run rows; its capture check is NL-79's.

## [NL-23] platform: `Dockerfile.web`, `Dockerfile.node`, full Compose stack (Postgres unpublished, internal token), committed `render.yaml` (PD-15 D)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Platform work, no US of its own: the demo runs locally under Docker Compose with the deploy config committed (PD-15 option D: no new hosting spend). This ticket makes the three Node processes and Postgres start together, migrate once, record that they started, and keep the database and secrets off the host and out of the images.

### What to build
Root files (A0): `Dockerfile.web`, `Dockerfile.node`, `docker-compose.yml` (replaces NL-01's Postgres-only file), `.dockerignore`, `.env.example`, `render.yaml`, `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh`; and, in each app, one start-event helper.
**Images (DO-3 §1; AD-15).** `Dockerfile.web`: Node 24, multi-stage, Next standalone output of `apps/web`, non-root user. `Dockerfile.node`: one image for `apps/worker` and `apps/collab`, two entry points selected by `command`. No `ENV` or `ARG` carries a secret; `.dockerignore` excludes `.git`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `evals/local/`, `docs/source/restricted/` (GR-9) and test output.
**Compose.** Services `web` (3000), `worker`, `collab` (1234, published: the browser's socket channel), `postgres` (16, named volume, healthcheck, **no `ports`**), one internal network, `depends_on` on Postgres health. `COLLAB_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, `AUDIT_HASH_SALT`, `DATABASE_URL` are required from the environment (`${VAR:?set it}`); provider keys appear by name only (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`), supplied at launch by `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env --project-env .env -- docker compose up`; `MODEL_PROVIDER_MODE` defaults to `stub`. `docker-compose.test.yml` (NL-01) keeps working and is the only place Postgres is published (127.0.0.1:55440). `.env.example` lists names and safe local values only.
**Start-up.** `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` runs `npm run db:migrate` (NL-08) once, then `exec`s the process. Each entry point calls its helper (`apps/web/instrumentation.ts` `register()`, `apps/worker/src/start-event.ts`, `apps/collab/src/start-event.ts`), which writes one `ops_event` (`kind process_start`, `service`, `build_id` from `resolve_build_id`) through `record_ops_event` (NL-08) once the database answers; a failure to write is logged, not fatal. This is the one edit this ticket makes to NL-06/NL-07 files (`main.ts`: one call), both A0.
**`render.yaml` (committed, not provisioned).** Per the workspace hosting default: web (Docker web service), worker (Docker background worker), collab (Docker web service), Postgres (Basic), region Ohio, `autoDeploy false`, secrets via an environment group `ls-secrets` (`fromGroup`), Postgres `ipAllowList: []`. The hosting-default rule's monthly lines are cited in a header comment; nothing is created on Render.
Must not: publish Postgres, put a key or token in a Dockerfile, image layer, compose file or `render.yaml`, copy `docs/source/restricted/` into any image, or call the Render API.

## [NL-24] web-ui: generated API client, Prism mock harness, mock collaboration server, app frame (nav, session redirect, can't-load and stale conventions), dialog and editor shells; SCR-1 sign in

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-37 — As a reviewer, author or approver (P-1, P-2, P-3), I need to sign in with an allow-listed staff email and see the actions my role can do. Platform work: every frontend ticket (NL-55…NL-76) builds on the client, mock harness, frame and shells made here, so none of them waits for a backend ticket.

### What to build
**1. Generated client (DO-3 §2.3 `api-client.ts`, §10).** `npm run api:types` runs `openapi-typescript docs/contracts/interface.openapi.yaml -o apps/web/src/lib/api-types.ts` (must equal `docs/contracts/generated/api-types.ts`). `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`: one typed client over `paths` (e.g. `openapi-fetch`), base URL from `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` (empty = same origin; Prism in mock mode), `credentials: "same-origin"`. Every non-2xx becomes `ApiError { status, code: ApiErrorCode, message, details, requestId }` read from the OpenAPI `Error` envelope; a non-envelope body or a network failure becomes the client-only code `NETWORK`. `UNAUTHENTICATED` on any `(app)` page redirects to `/sign-in?next=<path>`. No hand-built URLs anywhere. `src/lib/keys.ts` maps readable keys (`g6-u4` ↔ `G6.U4`, `L4` ↔ `G6.U4.L4`, IA §3).
**2. Prism mock harness.** Script `mock:api` = `npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock docs/contracts/interface.openapi.yaml -p 4010`; a Playwright `mock` project starts Prism and `next dev` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4010`. `apps/web/src/test-utils/` gives every screen ticket: `signInAs(page, role)` (the `getSession` example per role), `mockOperation(page, operationId, { code, example })` (Prism `Prefer` header, non-production only), `respondWithError(page, operationId, code, details?)` (a `page.route` answer typed by `components['schemas']['Error']` where the OpenAPI has no example for that code), `renderWithSession(ui, role)` for Vitest.
**3. Mock collaboration server** (`apps/web/mocks/collab-mock.ts`, script `mock:collab`, port 4020): an in-memory Hocuspocus server, no Postgres, speaking `x-collaboration-channel`'s message shapes — Yjs sync and awareness; `stored {content_hash, state_vector, stored_at}` ≤ 2 s after the last update; test controls `POST /__mock/lock` (broadcast `mode {read_only, state: submitted}`, then answer each further update with `refused {code: LESSON_LOCKED, message, refused_from}`), `/__mock/unlock`, `/__mock/drop` (close sockets → client `DISCONNECTED`); an upgrade without the mock `ls_session` cookie is refused. Lets NL-63 prove SP-2's editor rule without NL-80.
**4. App frame.** `app/(app)/layout.tsx` on FW-3's AppShell: nav (Units, Unit board, Prompt guidance for authors; entries flagged by cut number in `src/features/frame/nav.ts` so a fired cut hides its entry), top bar with breadcrumb slot, name, role and **Sign out** (`signOut`). Session gate via `getSession` → `src/features/frame/session-context.tsx` (`useSession()` → `{ user, role }`); `src/lib/roles.ts` `can(role, action)` for presentation only (the server decides). Shared conventions (SCREEN_SPECS *Conventions*) in `src/features/frame/`: `CantLoad`, `NotFound`, `StaleBanner`, `ForbiddenBanner` (repeats the server's sentence, nothing changes), `RoleNote`, `DisabledReason`; `src/lib/use-poll.ts` (2 s cadence, stale after > 10 s of failures, data kept with its time, never moves focus); `src/lib/announce.tsx` (polite, debounced live region, design.md §5 rule 7); `src/lib/draft-memory.ts` (UXQ-1: typed dialog text survives a re-sign-in on the same page).
**5. Shells handed over** (each renders its frame and a placeholder; the named ticket owns the file afterwards): `src/features/start-run/start-run-dialog.tsx` `StartRunDialog({ outlineVersionId, open, onClose })` → NL-58 · `src/features/insert-quote/insert-quote-dialog.tsx` `InsertQuoteDialog({ lessonId, slotId, open, onClose })` → NL-65 · `src/features/resolve/resolve-dialog.tsx` `ResolveDialog({ lessonId, mode: "resolve" | "clear_flag", issueId?, flagId?, open, onClose })` → NL-66 · `src/features/send-back/send-back-dialog.tsx` `SendBackDialog({ lessonId, mode: "request_changes" | "reopen", pin, open, onClose })` → NL-69 · `src/features/assist/assist-panel.tsx` `AssistPanel({ lessonId, selection, onClose })` → NL-72 · `src/editor/lesson-editor.tsx` `LessonEditor({ lessonId, lesson, readOnly, onClientState })` → NL-63 · `src/features/workspace/actions/action-bar.tsx` `WorkspaceActionBar({ lesson, issues, clientState })` and `use-review-heartbeat.ts` `useReviewHeartbeat({ lessonId, versionId })` → NL-64.
**6. SCR-1 Sign in** (`app/sign-in/**`, `src/features/sign-in/**`): no app shell; the card per SCR-1 *Layout* with **Staff email** and a password field (CON-1 System choice: email + password on seeded accounts), **Sign in**, the staff note, and the demo-accounts `well` listing the three seeded roles (demo builds only). Landing: author → `/units`, reviewer and approver → `/units/g6-u4/board`, or a same-origin relative `next`.
Must not: call a route outside the OpenAPI, edit `docs/contracts/**`, render any string as HTML, or ship `mocks/**` / `test-utils/**` in a production bundle. New dependencies (`openapi-fetch`, `openapi-typescript`, `@stoplight/prism-cli`, `@hocuspocus/server`, `@hocuspocus/provider`, `yjs`, `@axe-core/playwright` if absent) go to the batch merge agent (A0 owns `apps/web/package.json`).

## [NL-25] auth: seeded-account sign-in, session resolve, sign-out, `middleware.ts`; fills auth wiring

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or

### Story
US-37 — As a reviewer, author or approver (P-1, P-2, P-3), I need to sign in with an allow-listed staff email and password and be recognised by every later request, so that I see and do only what my role allows. Without this none of the other 23 routes can tell who is asking.

### What to build
**1. Repository (DO-3 §2.2 `packages/db/src/repos/sessions.ts`, DO-4 §3.5).** `PgSessionRepo implements SessionRepo` built from `PgRepo_ctor{db, ids, clock}`: `find_user_by_email(email)` (case-insensitive on the stored lower-cased email; returns `AppUserCredentials` with the scrypt `password_hash`), `create_session(user_id, token_hash, expires_at, tx)`, `resolve(token_hash, now)` (null when unknown, `expires_at <= now` or `revoked_at` set), `revoke(token_hash, now)` (sets `revoked_at`; idempotent). Tables `app_user` and `app_session` exist from NL-08 (`0001_identity.sql`); this ticket writes no DDL.
**2. Passwords (`apps/web/src/server/http/passwords.ts`, DO-4 §5).** `hash_password(password)` → self-describing scrypt string (`scrypt$N$r$p$salt_b64$hash_b64`, random 16-byte salt, `node:crypto` only); `verify_password(stored_hash, password)` → boolean, constant time (`timingSafeEqual`), false on any malformed stored hash, never throws. Pure functions with no web imports, so NL-82 (seed) can import or relocate them (slice plan Open item 2: DO-3's path is used here; moving them is a DO-3 `CHG` that NL-82 raises, not this ticket).
**3. Service (`apps/web/src/server/services/session-service.ts`, DO-4 §5 `SessionService`).** Constructor exactly as DO-4: `(sessions, audit, tx, clock, ids, settings)`. `sign_in(req, meta)`: unknown email → `DomainRefusal(NOT_ON_ALLOW_LIST)`; wrong password → `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`; each of the two failures first awaits `clock.sleep(1000)` (CON-1: failed sign-ins wait ~1 s) and writes **no row** (shared guarantee 2): one application-log line with `request_id`, the error code and `email_hash = sha256(AUDIT_HASH_SALT + lower(email))`, never the email or the password. Success: a random 32-byte token (`crypto.randomBytes`), only `sha256(token)` stored, `expires_at = now + SESSION_TTL_HOURS` (12 h [A], fixed at issue: DO-4 has no touch method, so there is no sliding renewal), and in the same `tx.with_tx` one `audit_event` (`action "session.sign_in"`, `target_kind "session"`, `target_id` = the first 16 hex characters of the token hash, `details` ids only, `request_id`). Returns `SignInOutcome{session, cookie_token, expires_at}`. `require(cookie_token, request_id)` → `RequestUser` or `UNAUTHENTICATED` (this is the `SessionResolver` implementation NL-13's `with_route` calls). `get_session(user)` → OpenAPI `Session`. `sign_out(user, cookie_token)` → `revoke` plus an `audit_event` `session.sign_out` in one transaction.
**4. Routes (`apps/web/app/api/session/route.ts`)** thin, via `with_route` (NL-13): `POST` → `signIn` (public: the one route that runs without a session; the Origin check still applies), `GET` → `getSession`, `DELETE` → `signOut`. The `ls_session` cookie is set on sign-in with `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Max-Age = SESSION_TTL_HOURS×3600` and `Secure` whenever `APP_ORIGIN` is not `http://localhost`/`127.0.0.1`; cleared on sign-out. The request schema is the strict Zod mirror `SignInRequest` (email, password): an extra key such as `synthetic` is `INVALID_REQUEST` (`synthetic` is seed-only, CON-1). If the merged `with_route` has no public-operation switch for `signIn`, stop and raise it: do not edit `apps/web/src/server/http/with-route.ts` (NL-13 owns it).
**5. `apps/web/middleware.ts`** (Next.js): a page request without the `ls_session` cookie is redirected (307) to `/sign-in?next=<url-encoded path+query>`; matcher excludes `/sign-in`, `/api/**`, `/_next/**`, `/healthz`, `/favicon.ico` and static assets. It checks cookie presence only; the server decides validity on the first API call (a stale cookie lands on the UNAUTHENTICATED path of NL-24's client).
**6. Wiring (`apps/web/src/server/wiring/sessions.ts`, the stub NL-06 created; DO-4 names the function `wire_sessions`)**: builds `PgSessionRepo`, `PgAuditLog` (NL-12), `SessionService` from `WebDeps` and returns `SessionWiring{sessions}`. `container.ts` is not edited (slice plan *Composition-root wiring owners*).
Must not: store or log a raw token, password or email on a refusal; add any route that sets `synthetic` or changes a role; render any string as HTML; edit `with-route.ts`, `container.ts`, `package.json` or any DDL.

## [NL-26] intake: upload and public-sheet import as numbered, hashed versions; Sheets fetcher; outline/standard repos; fills intake wiring

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or

### Story
US-1 and US-2 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to upload the unit outline as CSV or XLSX, or paste a public Google Sheet link, and get a numbered, hashed version, so that every run can say exactly which outline it came from and re-uploading never touches a lesson.

### What to build
**1. Repositories (DO-3 §2.2 `packages/db/src/repos/outlines.ts`, DO-4 §3.5).** `PgOutlineRepo implements OutlineRepo` and `PgStandardRepo implements StandardRepo`, both from `PgRepo_ctor`. This ticket implements `list_units`, `insert_version`, `version`, `rows`, `choices` (read), `links` and `row_context`; the three choice-writing methods `upsert_choice`, `mark_confirmed`, `generate_gate_inputs` are left as stubs that throw `NotBuiltYet("NL-77")` (NL-77 fills them in the same file, slice plan W4 row). `insert_version(v, outline, links, tx)` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock('outline:'||unit_id)`, numbers the version `max(number)+1`, stores `outline_version`, one `outline_row` per `NormalizedRow` (with `row_hash` = sha256 of its canonical JSON) and the `lesson_link` rows in the caller's transaction; two near-simultaneous uploads therefore get two distinct numbers. `PgStandardRepo.index()` builds NL-15's `StandardsIndex` from the `standard` table; `texts(codes)` returns `StandardRow`s.
**2. Fetcher (`apps/web/src/server/adapters/google-sheets.ts`, DO-4 §3.2).** `GoogleSheetsExportFetcher implements SheetFetcher` from `GoogleSheetsExportFetcher_ctor{timeout_ms = SHEETS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, max_bytes = OUTLINE_MAX_BYTES}`. `fetch_export(sheet_url)` accepts only `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/…` (any other scheme, host, port or userinfo → `INVALID_REQUEST` with `details.fields = ["sheet_url"]`, so the server never fetches an address a user chose), builds the export URL itself (`https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/export?format=xlsx`), makes **one** GET with redirects handled by hand: a redirect to any host other than `docs.google.com`/`doc-*.googleusercontent.com`, to an `accounts.google.com` sign-in page, or a 401/403 is `SHEET_NOT_PUBLIC`; a timeout or network error is `SHEET_UNREACHABLE`; the body is streamed and aborted past `max_bytes` (`UNSUPPORTED_FILE`, `details.reason "too_large"`). Returns `FetchedSheet{url, kind, data, sha256, fetched_at}`. No retry.
**3. Service (`apps/web/src/server/services/outline-service.ts`, DO-4 §5 `OutlineService`).** Create the file with the **full** DO-4 constructor `(outlines, standards, sheets, audit, tx, ids, clock, settings)` so NL-77 adds `report` and `record_choice` without changing it. `list_units(user)` → `UnitList` (each unit: `unit_id`, `unit_key` e.g. `g6-u4`, `title` "Grade 6 · Unit 4", `versions` newest first, `latest_run {run_id,state}|null` read through `RunRef` from the `run` table by a single read). `upload(user, file, unit_id)`: size over `OUTLINE_MAX_BYTES` or not CSV/XLSX (by content, not only by name) → `UNSUPPORTED_FILE` with `details.reason` `too_large`|`type`; `parse_workbook` → `normalize_outline(grid, await standards.index(), OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS)` (`HEADER_NOT_FOUND` with `details.columns_looked_for`, `TOO_MANY_ROWS`) → `compute_lesson_links` → one `tx.with_tx`: file under the unit the sheet writes (`unit_as_written` + grade, e.g. `G6.U4`; a conflicting filename unit is left for CON-4's `confirm_unit`, never moves the version), `insert_version` (`source_kind upload_csv|upload_xlsx|sheet_link`), `same_as_version` = the lowest earlier version number with the same sha256 (or null), `changed_lessons` = number of lesson rows whose `row_hash` differs from, or is absent in, version N-1 (0 for a first version or an identical re-upload), and one `audit_event` (`outline.upload` or `outline.import`, `target_kind "outline_version"`, `version_hash` = sha256, `details` ids and counts only). `import_link(user, req)` → `fetch_export` once, then the same path with `source_kind sheet_link`; the sheet is never fetched again for that version (the stored rows and sha256 are the record).
**4. Routes (thin, `with_route`):** `apps/web/app/api/units/route.ts` (`GET`, all roles), `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/route.ts` (`POST` multipart, author only), `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/import/route.ts` (`POST`, author only). Request parts parse with the Zod mirrors from NL-11 (`ImportLinkRequest`).
**5. Wiring (`apps/web/src/server/wiring/outlines.ts`, A0's stub; DO-4 `wire_outlines`)** builds the repos, `GoogleSheetsExportFetcher`, `PgAuditLog` and `OutlineService`; returns `OutlineWiring{outlines}`.
Must not: store or echo cell text as HTML; follow a redirect off the allow-listed hosts; keep the uploaded bytes outside the version's rows and hash; call a model; edit `container.ts`, `package.json` or DDL; implement report or choice behaviour (NL-77).

### Sources
- DO-4 §3.2 `SheetFetcher`, `FetchedSheet`; §3.5 `OutlineRepo`, `NewOutlineVersion`, `OutlineVersionRow`, `OutlineRowRecord`, `RowContext`, `StandardRepo`; §5 `OutlineService`, `UploadedFile`; §8 *intake* (`parse_workbook`, `normalize_outline`, `compute_lesson_links`); §12 `GoogleSheetsExportFetcher_ctor`, `wire_outlines`
- DO-3 §2.2, §2.3 (`outline-service.ts`, `google-sheets.ts`), §6 (`unit`, `outline_version`, `outline_row`, `lesson_link`), §7 (`OUTLINE_MAX_BYTES`, `OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS`, `SHEETS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`)
- CON-2 (agreed: `listUnits`, `uploadOutline`, `importOutlineLink`; `SHEET_NOT_PUBLIC`, `SHEET_UNREACHABLE`, `UNSUPPORTED_FILE`, `HEADER_NOT_FOUND`, `TOO_MANY_ROWS`; unit-matching and same-bytes guarantees); INTERFACE shared guarantees 1, 2, 6; PRD R-1, R-2, R-3, GR-5, R-58; TB-5
- WP-5 (`docs/data/worked-pairs.md`: issued sheet, same bytes twice); DO-6 WF-2; DO-5 S1; slice plan *Collision map* W3 (units and outline-version routes NL-26) and W4 (NL-77 adds methods only)
- **Brief check:** serves "upload the unit outline and generate lessons from it" (the issued brief's intake step); touches nothing out of scope (no re-fetch, no model call); weakens nothing → proceed.

- [ ] AC-3 [failure/refusal] Given a file that is not CSV/XLSX, one over 5 MB, one with no header row, one over 200 rows and a private sheet link, then 422 `UNSUPPORTED_FILE` (`details.reason` `type`), 422 `UNSUPPORTED_FILE` (`too_large`), 422 `HEADER_NOT_FOUND` (`details.columns_looked_for`), 422 `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, 422 `SHEET_NOT_PUBLIC`, and `outline_version`, `outline_row` and `audit_event` counts are unchanged each time (WF-2) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/route.test.ts -t refusals_write_nothing` — evidence: 5 responses; counts before == after — covers: R-2, CON-2, CON-G2
- [ ] AC-4 [failure/refusal] Given the fetcher times out (fake clock, 10 s) or the network fails, then 502 `SHEET_UNREACHABLE` and nothing is stored — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/adapters/google-sheets.test.ts -t unreachable` — evidence: response; no rows — covers: R-2, CON-2
- [ ] AC-5 [negative] The fetcher refuses to contact an address the caller chose: `http://169.254.169.254/`, `https://docs.google.com.evil.example/spreadsheets/d/x`, `https://user@docs.google.com/…`, `file:///etc/passwd` and a redirect from docs.google.com to `https://evil.example/` each give `INVALID_REQUEST` or `SHEET_NOT_PUBLIC` and the fake transport records zero requests to any non-Google host — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/adapters/google-sheets.test.ts -t no_ssrf` — evidence: 5 passing cases; transport log has only docs.google.com — covers: R-2, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] A private sheet (sign-in redirect, 401, 403) gives `SHEET_NOT_PUBLIC` with the plain message "share it publicly or upload the file" and no stack trace in the body; the response body for every refusal contains only `error.code`, `message`, `details` — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/adapters/google-sheets.test.ts -t private_sheet` — evidence: 3 passing cases — covers: R-2, CON-G6
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] The link's bytes are fetched once: after a successful import, `fetch_export` was called exactly once for that version and no later code path has a fetcher dependency (the stored rows are read instead) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/server/services/outline-service.test.ts -t fetched_once` — evidence: call count 1 — covers: R-2, CON-2
- [ ] AC-8 [failure/refusal] Given a reviewer or approver session, `POST /outline-versions` and `POST /outline-versions/import` return 403 `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` and write nothing; `GET /units` returns 200 for all three roles — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/route.test.ts -t roles` — evidence: 3 roles × 3 routes — covers: R-54, CON-G1
- [ ] AC-9 [negative] Given a cell containing `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` and a filename `../../etc/x.csv`, then the stored row and every response carry the cell as inert text (no markup interpretation) and the filename is never used as a path — verify: `npx vitest run apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/route.test.ts -t hostile_cell_and_filename` — evidence: stored text equals input; no fs write outside the test dir — covers: R-58, CON-G6

### Story
US-6 — As an outline author (P-2), I need to choose which rows to generate, see the prompt version the run will use, and set a spend cap, then start the run, so that a unit is generated once, under a ceiling, from a pinned prompt and a pinned set of intake choices.

### What to build
**1. Pure run machine (`packages/core/src/lifecycle/run-machine.ts`, DO-4 §8 *lifecycle*).** `derive_run_state(jobs, run: RunStateInput)`: `cancelled` flag → `cancelled`; `capped` → `capped`; `paused` → `paused`; plan not stored → `planning`; every lesson/candidate job terminal and all `ready` → `complete`; every job terminal with at least one `generation_failed` or cancelled → `partial`; otherwise `running`. `tile_state(job)`: `queued`→`queued`, `running`→ the job's stored step (`planning|drafting|checking|repairing`), `ready`→`ready`, `generation_failed`/`cancelled`→`failed` (OpenAPI `TileState`). `decide_run_control(current, action)` (CON-7): `cancel` from planning/running/paused → `cancelled`, `cancel_jobs true`; `retry_failed` only from `partial` → `running`, `requeue_failed true`; `resume` only from `paused` → `running`; anything else, and any action on `cancelled`, `capped` or `complete`, → `INVALID_TRANSITION`. Pure: no I/O, no clock.
**2. Run repository (`packages/db/src/repos/runs.ts`, DO-4 §3.5).** `PgRunRepo implements RunRepo` with every method of the port (NL-30, NL-31 and NL-78 use the others): `insert_run`, `get`, `find_by_idempotency_key(user_id, key, within_hours)`, `lock_for_update` (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), `set_state`, `mark_capped` (state `capped` + `capped_by`, one statement), `pinned_choices` (reads `run.choices_json`), `mark_plan_failed` (run → `paused`, `paused_check "unit_plan"`), `store_unit_plan` (sets `unit_plan.entries_json`, `state stored`, `run.plan_stored_at`, run `running`, in one transaction), `unit_plan`, `summary_rows`, `active_runs`. Tables `run`, `unit_plan` from NL-08.
**3. Service (`apps/web/src/server/services/run-service.ts`, DO-4 §5 `RunService`).** Create the file with the **full** DO-4 constructor `(runs, queue, outlines, states, prompts, spend, calls, audit, tx, ids, clock, settings)` so NL-78 adds `progress`, `control`, `plan`, `summary` without touching it (those methods throw `NotBuiltYet("NL-78")` here). `start(user, req, idempotency_key)` in this order (INTERFACE shared guarantee 11, then CON-5's list): author only; a repeated `Idempotency-Key` within `IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_H` (24) for the same user returns the first run and starts nothing (taken under `pg_advisory_xact_lock('run:start:'||user||key)`); `INVALID_REQUEST` for a trial without `lesson_id`, `rows` naming a row that is not a lesson row, `unfinished_of_run` naming a run of another outline version, `cap_usd <= 0`; `NOT_FOUND` for an unknown outline version or prompt version; `VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE` (`details.errors_unconfirmed`) from `generate_gate(outlines.generate_gate_inputs(...))`; `DAY_CAP_REACHED` (`details.scope` `user`|`project`, `details.remaining_usd`) from `spend.check_day_cap(user_id, cap_usd)`. Then **one** `tx.with_tx`: `insert_run` with the pinned prompt version, the copied intake choices and `choices_hash` (sha256 of their canonical JSON), the lesson links copied into the run's `unit_plan` row, `idempotency_key`; `states.ensure_lessons(rows_in_scope, unit_id)`; `queue.create_run_jobs` (a full run: one `unit_plan` job plus one `lesson` job per lesson in scope; a trial: one `candidate` job, no plan job) with each job's `idempotency_key = sha256(run_id, lesson_id, prompt_version_id, schema_version)`; one `audit_event` `run.start`. After commit it issues `NOTIFY lesson_job`. Returns the OpenAPI `Run` (`state "planning"`, `spent_usd 0`). The dialog's suggested cap comes from `run_cap_for` (NL-35) and is not computed here.
**4. Route (`apps/web/app/api/runs/route.ts`)**: `POST` via `with_route` (author, `StartRunRequest`, success 201), reading the `Idempotency-Key` header. The service object comes from `getWebServices().runs`; the wiring file `wiring/runs.ts` is NL-78's, so this ticket's route tests inject a service built from fakes.
Must not: start a lesson job before a plan exists (the queue enforces it, NL-28); write a spend row; call a model; edit `container.ts`, `wiring/runs.ts`, `package.json`, DDL, `prompt-service.ts`.

### Story
US-8 — As an outline author (P-2), I need a run to survive a worker restart and failed lessons to be retried on their own, so that a killed worker costs at most the calls in flight and no lesson is stored or paid for twice. This ticket is the queue underneath that promise.

### What to build
**Module:** `packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.ts` — `PgJobQueue implements JobQueue` (DO-4 §3.4) from `PgRepo_ctor{db, ids, clock}`; table `lesson_job` (NL-08 `0004_runs.sql`; this ticket writes no DDL). It is the riskiest SQL in the product (HP-7), so every method is one statement or one short transaction and has an integration test. Runs are created in tests by a raw-SQL fixture helper (`packages/db/src/testing/seed-run.ts`, this ticket's), because `PgRunRepo` is NL-27's, same wave.
- `create_run_jobs(jobs, tx)` bulk-inserts `NewJob`s as `queued` (`queued_at = clock.now()`), `ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING`; returns the number inserted. `create_candidate_job(job, tx)` inserts one (with `NewJob.reviewer_note` into `lesson_job.reviewer_note`; DO-4 §3.4, DO-3 §6, §13 R-15) and returns its `JobRow`; `claim` copies `reviewer_note` onto `ClaimedJob`; the partial unique index (one queued or running candidate job per lesson, NL-08) turns a second into `DomainRefusal(INVALID_TRANSITION, details.reason "candidate_in_flight")`.
- `claim(worker_id, max_active_runs, lease_ms)`: in one statement with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, picks from the active runs (state `planning` or `running`, at most `max_active_runs` of them, oldest first) the run with the fewest running jobs, and inside it the oldest queued job (`queued_at`, then `job_id`). `lesson` jobs are claimable only when the run's `plan_stored_at` is set (R-8); `unit_plan` and `candidate` jobs are not gated. Sets `status running`, `attempt = attempt + 1`, `worker_id`, `lease_until = now + lease_ms`, `started_at` if null, `tile_state` to `planning` (unit_plan) or `drafting`; returns `ClaimedJob` (with `unit_id`, `prompt_version_id`, `schema_version`, `outline_version_id`, `started_by`, `idempotency_key` read from the run row, G-23) or null. Jobs of `paused`, `capped` or `cancelled` runs are never claimed.
- `renew_lease(job_id, lease_ms)`: extends only a job that is still `running` with a lease not yet lapsed; returns false otherwise (taken over or requeued).
- `set_tile_state(job_id, tile_state)`; `finish(outcome)`: only on a `running` job (a second finish is a no-op), sets `status`, `tile_state`, `failure_reasons_json`, `brakes_fired`, `repairs`, `truncation_retries`, `retries`, `cost_usd`, `finished_at`, and sets `calls_lost` to the count of this job's `model_call` rows with `status 'lost'` (read-only access to that table; nothing else writes `calls_lost`).
- `requeue_expired(now)`: `running` jobs with `lease_until < now` → `queued` (attempt kept, `worker_id` cleared); returns `RequeueReport{requeued, job_ids}`. It touches only `lesson_job`; marking lost calls and releasing reservations belong to `ClaimLoop.start` (NL-30).
- `requeue_failed(run_id, tx)`: only `generation_failed` jobs of the run → `queued`, failure fields cleared; ready jobs are untouched; returns the count. `cancel_run(run_id, reason, tx)`: queued jobs → `cancelled`, tile `failed`, `failure_reasons [{check: reason}]` (`cancelled`|`capped`); running jobs are left to finish (they stop at their next node through `is_cancelled`); returns the count. `jobs_for_run(run_id)` → `JobRow[]`. `is_cancelled(job_id)` → true when the job is `cancelled` or its run's state is `cancelled` (not for `capped`: in-flight calls finish).
Must not: write `model_call`, `spend_reservation`, `run` or `lesson` rows; call a model; add a migration.

- DO-3 §2.2 (`repos/job-queue.ts`), §6 (`lesson_job` columns and the candidate partial unique index), §7 (`MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS`, `JOB_LEASE_MS`)
- CON-5 (jobs idempotent per run/lesson/prompt/schema; never refused for load), CON-6 (restart guarantees; cancelled/capped tiles of unstarted jobs have no lesson), CON-7 (retry only failed; cancel stops new calls), CON-16 (one candidate in flight per lesson); HP-7 (`docs/design/hard-problems.md`) mechanics 1–4; PRD R-16, R-8; capacity doc (fair share, ≤ 6 jobs, ≤ 3 runs)
- DO-5 S6; DO-6 WF-22, WF-6, WF-28; slice plan *Collision map* W3 (`job-queue.ts` NL-28)
- **Brief check:** serves "durable, idempotent generation jobs in a separate worker with retries" (R-16, the brief's long-running-job requirement); touches nothing out of scope (no model call); weakens nothing → proceed.

- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given a lesson job whose run has `plan_stored_at` null, `claim` returns null; after the plan is stored the same call returns the job; a `unit_plan` job and a `candidate` job are claimable without a plan (R-8) — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t lesson_jobs_wait_for_plan` — evidence: 3 results — covers: R-8, R-16
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Given active run A with 2 running jobs and run B with 0, `claim` returns B's job; given four active runs and `max_active_runs 3`, the fourth run's jobs are never claimed; inside one run the oldest queued job goes first; jobs of paused, capped and cancelled runs are never claimed — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t fair_share_and_active_run_cap` — evidence: claimed `run_id` list matches expectation — covers: R-16, CON-5
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] Given a `running` job with a lapsed lease, `requeue_expired(now)` returns `RequeueReport{requeued 1, job_ids [that job]}`, the job is `queued` with `attempt` unchanged, and an ordinary running job with a live lease is untouched; `model_call` and `spend_reservation` rows are not modified — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t expired_lease_requeues` — evidence: report and rows before/after — covers: R-16, CON-6, OBS-2
- [ ] AC-5 [failure/refusal] `renew_lease` returns true for a live running job and false for a requeued, finished or lapsed one; a second `finish` on the same job changes nothing (no second `finished_at`, counters unchanged) — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t renew_and_finish_guards` — evidence: booleans; row unchanged — covers: R-16, CON-6
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] `finish` stores status, tile, failure reasons (`{check, check_kind?, message}` list), brakes fired, repairs, truncation retries, retries and cost, and sets `calls_lost` to the number of the job's `lost` `model_call` rows (2 seeded → 2) — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t finish_records_counters` — evidence: row read back — covers: R-16, M-15
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] `requeue_failed` re-queues only `generation_failed` jobs of the run (ready jobs, cancelled jobs and other runs' jobs untouched) and returns the count; the ready jobs' rows are byte-identical before and after (WF-6) — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t retry_failed_only_failed` — evidence: count 2 of 5; hash of ready rows equal — covers: R-16, CON-7
- [ ] AC-8 [invariant] `cancel_run(run_id, "cancelled", tx)` marks queued jobs `cancelled`, tile `failed`, reason `[{check: cancelled}]` and leaves running jobs running; `is_cancelled` is true for the cancelled job and for a running job of a `cancelled` run, false for a running job of a `capped` run; `cancel_run(…, "capped")` records `capped` (WF-6) — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t cancel_run_and_is_cancelled` — evidence: rows and booleans — covers: R-16, CON-6, CON-7
- [ ] AC-9 [failure/refusal] A second `create_candidate_job` for a lesson with a queued or running candidate job throws `DomainRefusal(INVALID_TRANSITION)` with `details.reason "candidate_in_flight"` and inserts nothing; after the first finishes a new one is accepted — verify: `npx vitest run packages/db/src/repos/job-queue.int.test.ts -t one_candidate_per_lesson` — evidence: refusal then success — covers: CON-16

## [NL-29] generation: lesson/candidate job runner and nodes (reserve, draft, compile-check, one repair on required-block misses, truncation retry, store, settle, fail; safety flags at v1)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`

### Story
US-7 — As an outline author (P-2), I need each lesson to be drafted, checked, repaired at most once and stored as a numbered draft with its full provenance, or to fail with a stated reason, so that the board shows ready lessons I can open and honest reasons for the rest.

### What to build
**Modules (DO-3 §2.4, DO-4 §6):** `apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.ts` (`LessonJobRunner`) and `apps/worker/src/generation/nodes/{draft-node,compile-check-node,repair-node,store-node,fail-node}.ts`. TypeScript interfaces and constructors exactly as DO-4 §6 (`DraftNode`, `CompileCheckNode`, `RepairNode`, `StoreNode`, `FailNode`, `LessonJobRunner`, `LessonJobState`). All collaborators are DO-4 ports or earlier-wave real code; same-wave ones (`PaidCaller`/`ModelCallRecorder` NL-33, `LessonDocStore` NL-36, `CheckContextLoader` NL-38, `RunFinalizer` NL-30, `LessonVersionRepo`/`LessonStateRepo` NL-42, `SafetyFlagRepo` NL-43) are typed from DO-4 and tested with doubles. No node reserves or settles by itself: every call goes through `PaidCaller` (G-17, G-18), which reserves that call's own worst case right before sending it.
- **DraftNode.** `runs.pinned_choices(run_id)` → `outlines.row_context(outline_version_id, lesson_id, pinned)`; standards via `standards.texts(codes)`; plan entries (own and neighbours) from `runs.unit_plan(parent_run_id ?? run_id)` (a candidate run reuses its parent's plan, R-8); `renderer.render_lesson_draft(DraftPromptInput{prompt = prompts.get(job.prompt_version_id), …, template = SECTION_TEMPLATES[type], example_set_id null, reviewer_note = job.reviewer_note})` (the CON-16 regenerate note for a candidate job, null otherwise; DO-4 §3.4 `ClaimedJob.reviewer_note`, §13 R-15; never logged)`. First `recorder.checkpoint(job_id, "lesson_draft", 1)`: a stored completed output is used and **no call is sent**. Otherwise `PaidCaller.call` with alias `GENERATION`, `output_mode "prompt_embedded"`, `max_output_tokens DRAFT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP` (32000), `timeout_ms MODEL_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `effort MODEL_EFFORT`, `temperature null`, `ctx.attempt 1`, `purpose "lesson_draft"`, `user_id = job.started_by`. `stop_reason "max_tokens"` → one truncation retry (`purpose "truncation_retry"`, ordinal 1, `max_output_tokens TRUNCATION_RETRY_TOKEN_CAP` 48000, its own reservation; `truncation_retries 1`, not counted as the repair); truncated twice → brake `truncation_retry`, route to fail. `SpendRefused` → brake `spend_run_cap|spend_day_cap|spend_project_cap` and fail with no repair; a `ProviderError` that survived the recorder's retries → fail with its kind; `rate_limit_retries` is read from `RecordedCall.retries`.
- **CompileCheckNode.** Parse `raw_output` as JSON and validate with the Zod `LessonDraft` (issue paths only → `schema_issues`; no raw text in errors) → `compile_draft(draft, CompileContext{row, template, unit_id = job.unit_id, schema_version})` (`CompileError` → `compile_error`) → `loader.load(lesson_id, compiled.lesson, compiled.content_hash)` → `run_checks(ctx, CHECK_RULES, CHECK_POLICY)` → `check_result`; `check_passed` = no blocking finding.
- **Router.** `route_after_checks` (NL-22) decides `store` / `repair` / `fail` (`max_repair_rounds 1`; the repair gets the draft and only what failed).
- **RepairNode.** Alias `REPAIR` (`MODEL_REPAIR_ID`), `checkpoint(job, "repair", 1)` first, `render_repair(RepairPromptInput{draft_raw, failing findings, schema_issues, template})`, `PaidCaller.call` (`prompt_embedded`, `DRAFT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP`), `repair_rounds + 1`; then CompileCheckNode runs again and the router decides once more.
- **StoreNode** (one `tx.with_tx`, G-25). Lesson job: `versions.write_generated_version(NewGeneratedVersion{kind "generated", idempotency_key = job.idempotency_key, provenance{outline_row_hash, prompt_version_id, model = served model of the draft call, parameters {effort, max_output_tokens, output_mode}, schema_version, example_set_id null, run_id, model_call_ids = every call of the job in order, cost_usd = sum of the job's settled call costs, ai_assisted_spans 0, derived_from_version_id null}})`. `created false` → the earlier run already stored v1: return its version and write nothing else. `created true` → `docs.seed_initial(lesson_id, lesson, system actor, tx)` (seq 1 plus the coalesced `check_job` in the same transaction) + `flags.create_for_lesson(lesson_id, source_rows, tx)` + `states.set_state(lesson_id, "draft", null, tx)`. **Safety flags are written here** (DO-4 §6 `StoreNode`; this settles the slice plan's open item 3): `source_rows` are the outline row numbers whose `safety_note` segments the run's pinned choices confirmed (`confirm_safety_note`); none → no flag rows. Candidate job: `write_generated_version(kind "candidate", adopted false)` only; if the lesson is `generation_failed` and has no generated version the candidate becomes v1 the same way as a lesson job (CON-16).
- **FailNode.** `outcome.failure_reasons = failure_reasons_for(FailureInput)` (NL-22). Lesson job → `set_state(generation_failed)`. Candidate job → if `versions.has_generated_version(lesson_id)` the lesson state is **not** touched (an `in_review` lesson stays `in_review`); with no version it becomes `generation_failed`. A job refused before its first call (capped, cancelled) writes no lesson row (CON-6).
- **LessonJobRunner.run(job).** `queue.set_tile_state` at each step (`drafting`, `checking`, `repairing`); draft → compile_check → route → (repair → compile_check → route) → store | fail → `queue.finish(outcome)` → `finalizer.after_job(run_id, outcome)`. `queue.is_cancelled(job_id)` is read between nodes (cancelled → no further call, status `cancelled`); `settings.job_wall_clock_ms` (600000) is checked before each node (brake `job_wall_clock`, no further call); `LeaseLost` stops the job and leaves it to `requeue_expired`; a `SpendRefused` or surviving `ProviderError` goes straight to fail.
Must not: write `model_call` or `spend_reservation` rows itself; import the Anthropic SDK; write `issue` or `alignment_link` (the check worker does, NL-81); edit `run-finalizer.ts`/`claim-loop.ts` (NL-30), `unit-plan-job.ts` (NL-31), `wiring/generation.ts` (NL-79).

### Sources
- DO-4 §6 (`LessonJobState`, `RouteInput`, `route_after_checks`, `FailureInput`, `failure_reasons_for`, `DraftNode`, `CompileCheckNode`, `RepairNode`, `StoreNode`, `FailNode`, `LessonJobRunner`); §3.4 `ClaimedJob`, `JobOutcome`, `LessonDocStore.seed_initial`; §3.5 `NewGeneratedVersion`, `ProvenanceRecord`, `LessonVersionRepo`, `SafetyFlagRepo`; §4 `PaidCaller`, `ModelCallRecorder.checkpoint`, `DraftPromptInput`, `RepairPromptInput`; §8 *compile*, *checks*; §10.2
- DO-3 §2.4 (generation modules), §7 (`DRAFT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP`, `TRUNCATION_RETRY_TOKEN_CAP`, `MODEL_EFFORT`, `JOB_WALL_CLOCK_MS`, the no-setting row for temperature and example set), §6 (`lesson_version`, `lesson_doc`, `safety_flag`)
- CON-6 (reasons vocabulary, restart guarantees, unstarted tiles have no lesson row), CON-16 (candidate rules); PRD R-16, R-19 (one repair), R-12, R-21; SP-1 (`docs/analysis/spikes/SP-1.md`: one draft call + one repair, prompt-embedded schema, caps 32,000 / 48,000)
- WP-1, WP-2 (3-minute Look Back repaired once), WP-4 (content warning → safety flag); DO-5 S3, S6; DO-6 WF-22; slice plan *Collision map* W3 (`lesson-job-runner.ts` + `nodes/**` NL-29)
- **Brief check:** serves "generate each lesson with an LLM and persist it" with one bounded repair and honest failures; touches nothing out of scope (the model is behind PaidCaller); weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given `StubModelClient` scripted with a valid `LessonDraft` for WP-1 (row 8 → Lesson 4), when the runner runs the claimed job, then exactly one call has `purpose "lesson_draft"`, `alias GENERATION`, `output_mode prompt_embedded`, `max_output_tokens 32000`, and the job ends `status ready`, `tile_state ready`, `repairs 0`, with one `lesson_version` of `kind generated`, `lesson.state draft`, one `lesson_doc` `seq 1` and one `check_job` row (WF-22) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t wp1_happy_path` — evidence: job row, 1 call, 1 version, 1 doc, 1 check_job — covers: R-16, R-26, CON-6
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given WP-2/WP-1 with a stub draft whose Look Back section is 3 minutes, exactly one call has `purpose repair`, `alias REPAIR`; with a repaired draft that passes the job ends `ready` with `repairs 1`; the repair prompt contains the draft and only the failing findings (WF-22) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t one_repair_then_store` — evidence: 2 call rows; prompt asserted — covers: R-19, R-16, EV-S3
- [ ] AC-3 [failure/refusal] Given the repaired draft still fails `minutes_out_of_range`, then no second repair call exists, `lesson.state generation_failed`, and `failure_reasons` contains `{check: "check_failed", check_kind: "minutes_out_of_range"}` — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t still_failing_after_one_repair` — evidence: job row; repair-call count 1 — covers: R-19, CON-6
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] Given the stub returns `stop_reason max_tokens` first, a second call has `purpose truncation_retry` and `max_output_tokens 48000` with its own reservation, the job ends with `truncation_retries 1`, `repairs 0`; truncated twice → `generation_failed` with `{check: "truncated"}`, brake `truncation_retry`, and no third draft call — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t truncation_retry_and_twice` — evidence: call rows and counters for both cases — covers: R-16, CON-6
- [ ] AC-5 [failure/refusal] Given `FakeSpendLedger` refuses with `refused_by run_cap` (then `day_cap`, `project_cap`), no `model_call` row is written, `brakes_fired` contains `spend_run_cap` (`spend_day_cap`, `spend_project_cap`), `failure_reasons` is `[{check: "capped"}]`, there is no repair, and no lesson row is written for a job refused before its first call — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t reservation_refused_makes_no_call` — evidence: 3 job rows; zero call rows — covers: R-16, CON-6, EV-S6
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] Wall clock and cancel: with `FakeClock` past 600000 ms before the compile-check node, `brakes_fired` contains `job_wall_clock`, no further call, reason `timeout`; with `queue.is_cancelled` true after the draft node the job ends `cancelled`, no further call, no `lesson_version` — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t wall_clock_and_cancel` — evidence: 2 job rows; call counts — covers: R-16, CON-7
- [ ] AC-7 [failure/refusal] Given `renew_lease` false (`LeaseLost`), the runner stops, calls neither `queue.finish` nor any store, and writes no `lesson_version` — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/lesson-job-runner.test.ts -t lease_lost_stops_node` — evidence: no version row; finish not called — covers: R-16
- [ ] AC-8 [invariant] Checkpoint: given a completed `lesson_draft` call row already stored for `(job_id, "lesson_draft", 1)` (a requeued job), the draft node sends no new call and continues from the stored raw output; a requeue after the repair call likewise sends no second repair — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/nodes/draft-node.test.ts -t checkpoint_no_repay` — evidence: call-count 0 on the second run — covers: R-16, EV-S6, M-44
- [ ] AC-9 [invariant] Idempotent store: `StoreNode` run twice with the same `idempotency_key` leaves one `lesson_version`, one `lesson_doc` and one `check_job`, the second run returning the first version; v1, its `lesson_doc seq 1`, its flags and `lesson.state draft` commit in one transaction (a forced failure in `create_for_lesson` rolls back all) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/nodes/store-node.int.test.ts -t store_is_idempotent_and_atomic` (Postgres 16 test container; real repos where merged, else doubles) — evidence: counts 1/1/1; rollback case — covers: R-16, R-35, EV-S6
- [ ] AC-10 [invariant] Provenance and safety flags: the stored v1's `provenance.run_id == job.run_id`, `model_call_ids` lists the draft (and repair) calls in order, `cost_usd` equals the sum of the job's call costs, `example_set_id` is null; for WP-4 (row 39, confirmed safety note) one `safety_flag` row is created for the lesson with `source_row 39`, and for WP-1 none (WF-22) — verify: `npx vitest run apps/worker/src/generation/nodes/store-node.test.ts -t provenance_and_flags` — evidence: provenance JSON vs call rows; flag rows — covers: R-35, GR-8, GR-12, M-38

### Story
US-8 — As an outline author (P-2), I need the worker to keep at most six lessons in flight, to pick up exactly where a killed worker stopped, and to move a run to complete, partial, paused or capped by itself, so that a 47-lesson unit finishes without me watching it and a restart costs at most the calls in flight.

### What to build
**Modules (DO-3 §2.4, DO-4 §6):** `apps/worker/src/queue/claim-loop.ts` (`ClaimLoop`) and `apps/worker/src/generation/run-finalizer.ts` (`RunFinalizer`). Collaborators typed from DO-4 and tested with doubles where they are same-wave (`LessonJobRunner` NL-29, `UnitPlanJob` NL-31, `PgJobQueue` NL-28, `PgRunRepo` NL-27, `PgModelCallLog` NL-33, `PgSpendLedger` NL-35); `derive_run_state` is NL-27's pure code typed from DO-4 §8, `should_pause_run` is NL-22's.
- **ClaimLoop.start() → TickReport.** `queue.requeue_expired(clock.now())` once; for the returned `job_ids`, `calls.mark_lost(job_id)` for each (counted in `lost_calls_marked`) and `spend.release_for_jobs(job_ids)` (`reservations_released`) — in that order, before any claim (G-9). The report also carries `requeued_at_start`.
- **ClaimLoop.run_until(stop) → LoopExit.** Keeps up to `GENERATION_CONCURRENCY` (6, SP-1) jobs in flight with a counting semaphore. Each cycle: `queue.claim(settings.worker_id, MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS, JOB_LEASE_MS)`; a `unit_plan` job goes to `UnitPlanJob.run` and then `queue.finish` (status from `UnitPlanOutcome.stored`; a stored plan finishes `ready`; a failure finishes `generation_failed` with its `FailureReason`); a `lesson` or `candidate` job goes to `LessonJobRunner.run` (which finishes its own job). When nothing is claimable it `clock.sleep(JOB_POLL_MS)`. Lease renewal: every 30 s per in-flight job `queue.renew_lease`; false → that job is told to stop (`LeaseLost`) and the loop does not finish it. On `stop.is_set()` (SIGTERM) it stops claiming, waits for in-flight calls to finish, and returns `LoopExit{reason "sigterm", drained_jobs, abandoned_jobs}`; an `InvariantViolation` from a runner is logged at error level and returns `reason "fatal"`. `ClaimLoop` receives a `TxRunner` (DO-4 §6 constructor, §13 R-6), used only so that a run whose plan call was capped gets `queue.cancel_run(run_id, "capped", tx)` (DO-4's `UnitPlanJob` marks the run capped but nothing could cancel its queued lesson jobs).
- **RunFinalizer.after_job(run_id, outcome) → RunStateChange | None.** One `tx.with_tx`: if `outcome.brakes_fired` holds a `spend_*` brake → `runs.mark_capped(run_id, cap)` (`spend_run_cap→run_cap`, `spend_day_cap→day_cap`, `spend_project_cap→project_cap`) and `queue.cancel_run(run_id, "capped", tx)` (queued tiles `failed`, reason `capped`; in-flight jobs finish); else `should_pause_run(recent terminal jobs, CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SAME_CHECK = 3)` → `runs.set_state(run_id, "paused", check)`; else `derive_run_state(jobs_for_run, RunStateInput)` and `runs.set_state` only when it changed. A change to `complete`/`partial`/`capped`/`paused` is returned as `RunStateChange{from_state,to_state,paused_check}`; no change returns null. When the run reaches a terminal state it calls `completeness(run_id)` and logs a warning line `run.incomplete` for any gap.
- **RunFinalizer.completeness(run_id) → CompletenessReport.** `terminal_jobs_without_calls`: jobs `ready` or `generation_failed` with no `model_call` row, excluding jobs refused before their first call (reasons `capped` or `cancelled` and no lesson row); `summary_matches_calls`: `calls.totals_for_run(run_id).cost_usd` equals the run's settled spend (DO-6 missing-instrumentation checks 1 and 2).
Must not: run a node itself; write `lesson_version`, `lesson_doc` or `spend_reservation` rows; edit `lesson-job-runner.ts` (NL-29), `unit-plan-job.ts` (NL-31), `main.ts` or `wiring/generation.ts` (NL-07/NL-79).

### Sources
- DO-4 §6 (`ClaimLoop`, `TickReport`, `LoopExit`, `StopSignal`, `RunFinalizer`, `RunStateChange`, `CompletenessReport`, `UnitPlanOutcome`); §3.4 `JobQueue`, `ModelCallLog.mark_lost`, `SpendLedger.release_for_jobs`; §8 *lifecycle* (`derive_run_state`, `should_pause_run`, `PauseDecision`); §10.2 `LeaseLost`, `InvariantViolation`
- DO-3 §2.4 (`claim-loop.ts`, `run-finalizer.ts`), §7 (`GENERATION_CONCURRENCY`, `MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS`, `JOB_LEASE_MS`, `JOB_POLL_MS`, `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_SAME_CHECK`, `WORKER_ID`)
- CON-6 (run ends complete, partial, capped, paused; restart guarantees; spend never past cap), CON-7 (cancel: in-flight calls finish); HP-7 mechanics; PRD R-16 as amended; capacity doc (≤ 6 in flight, SP-1: 6 chosen)
- DO-5 S6 (47/47 terminal, zero re-paid calls); DO-6 WF-22, WF-6, *Missing instrumentation* 1–2; slice plan *Collision map* W3 (`run-finalizer.ts` + `queue/claim-loop.ts` NL-30)

## [NL-31] generation: UnitPlan job, stored before any lesson claim

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or

### Story
US-9 — As an outline author (P-2), I need one plan for the whole unit — a line for every teaching day with what it hands forward — written and stored before any lesson is drafted, so that lessons are written against one consistent plan and I can read it first.

### What to build
**Module:** `apps/worker/src/generation/unit-plan-job.ts` — `UnitPlanJob` (DO-4 §6), constructor `(paid, renderer, runs, outlines, prompts, settings)`. `run(job: ClaimedJob) → UnitPlanOutcome{run_id, stored, entries, model_call_id, failure}`.
1. **Input.** `runs.get(run_id)` (scope, outline version), `outlines.rows(outline_version_id)` filtered to the run's scope rows (all lesson and flex-day rows for scope `all`), the outline's unit rules from `outlines.row_context(ov, first_lesson_id, runs.pinned_choices(run_id)).unit_rules`, and `outlines.links(ov)` (the links the run copied at start; computed by code, never by the model, HP-1). `renderer.render_unit_plan(UnitPlanPromptInput{run_id, prompt = prompts.get(job.prompt_version_id), rows, unit_rules, links})`.
2. **Call.** `recorder.checkpoint(job_id, "unit_plan", 1)` first: a completed stored output is validated and used with **no new call**. Otherwise one `PaidCaller.call` (`purpose "unit_plan"`, alias `GENERATION`, `output_mode "schema_enforced"` because `UnitPlanDraft` compiles, SP-1; `max_output_tokens DRAFT_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP` since DO-3 §7 has no separate plan cap, `ctx.attempt 1`, `user_id = job.started_by`).
3. **Validate (Zod `UnitPlanDraft`, then code).** Exactly one entry per teaching day in scope, each `lesson_id` in scope, no duplicates, `day` ascending. A failure triggers **at most one repair**: the repair is one more `render_unit_plan` call with `repair_of = UnitPlanRepairNote{draft_raw, issues}` (the previous raw plan and the Zod paths and code checks that failed, as G-22 does for lessons; `purpose "repair"`, ordinal 1; DO-4 §4 `UnitPlanPromptInput`, §6 `UnitPlanJob`, §13 R-13). Still invalid → `runs.mark_plan_failed(run_id)` (run `paused`, `paused_check "unit_plan"`; Resume re-queues the job, CON-7) and `failure = schema_invalid`.
4. **Store.** Valid → `runs.store_unit_plan(run_id, plan, model_call_id)` (sets `plan_stored_at`, `unit_plan.state stored`, run `running` in one transaction, NL-27), which is what makes lesson jobs claimable (R-8, NL-28). The `lesson_link` rows already sit in the run's plan row from `startRun`; the model's hand-forward text stays advisory.
5. **Refusals.** `SpendRefused` → `runs.mark_capped(run_id, cap)`, `failure = capped`, no call row. A surviving `ProviderError` → `mark_plan_failed`, `failure` = its kind (`rate_limited`, `timeout`, `provider_error`).
Must not: store anything before validation passes; let a lesson job start first (the gate is `plan_stored_at`); write `lesson` rows; create jobs; edit `claim-loop.ts` or `run-finalizer.ts` (NL-30).

### Sources
