## [NL-77] intake: validation report read and intake choices (`default` vs confirmed by name)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-3 — As an author I need to see every problem in the outline before any money is spent, with Generate kept off until every error is confirmed, so that a bad code never reaches 47 paid model calls. US-4 and US-5 — I confirm what each cell really is and keep or re-map an ELD label, so that the lesson cites the state's standard.

### What to build
Add the two read/write halves of intake to the `OutlineService` that NL-26 created (same file, **methods only**; the constructor and `wiring/outlines.ts` do not change, slice plan *Composition-root wiring owners*):

- `OutlineService.report(user, outline_version_id) -> ValidationReport` (CON-3, `getValidationReport`): reads the stored rows and findings through `OutlineRepo.version / rows / choices` and returns `build_validation_report(version, outline, choices)` (DO-4 §8, NL-17). **Reads never write** (shared guarantee 5) and never call a model (HP-6). Also fills `runs_from_this_version` (run id, started_at, `choices_hash`, newest first, empty before the first run) and `generate_allowed` (true when `errors_unconfirmed == 0`, `generate_gate`).
- `OutlineService.record_choice(user, outline_version_id, req) -> IntakeChoiceResult` (CON-4, `recordIntakeChoice`): one tx via `TxRunner.with_tx`: role `author` only, target lookup, kind-vs-value validation, `OutlineRepo.upsert_choice` (status `default` or `confirmed`, `confirmed_by`), `OutlineRepo.mark_confirmed` the first time `generate_gate` allows, one `AuditLog.append`. `revert` restores the stored default. Returns the updated row, new counts and `generate_allowed`.
- Routes: `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/[outlineVersionId]/report/route.ts` (GET) and `.../choices/route.ts` (POST), both through `with_route` (NL-13 / NL-25: session, Origin check, Zod parse, role, then the service). The choices methods of `packages/db/src/repos/outlines.ts` (`upsert_choice`, `mark_confirmed`) are NL-26's file; add only those two methods if NL-26 left them as shells, otherwise do not touch it.

**Refusals (CON-3/CON-4):** `NOT_FOUND` (version or target), `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` (non-author on choices), `INVALID_CHOICE` 422 with `details.reason` (e.g. `edit_fix` to a code not in the standards list, a unit-rule scope naming a row outside the sheet), `INVALID_TRANSITION` 409 (`confirm_unit` with a different unit after a run started from this version). Error precedence per shared guarantee 11. A refusal writes no row of any kind, only one application-log line (shared guarantee 2).

**Must not:** call a model; recompute findings on read (they are stored at upload, NL-26); return cell text as markup (R-58); edit NL-26's upload/import code, `wiring/outlines.ts` or the standards data.

### Sources
- DO-4 §5 `OutlineService`, §8 *intake* (`build_validation_report`, `generate_gate`), §3.5 `OutlineRepo`, §10.1 (`INVALID_CHOICE`); DO-3 §2.3 (A4), §6 (`intake_choice`, `outline_version`).
- CON-3, CON-4 (agreed); shared guarantees 1, 2, 5, 11; OpenAPI `getValidationReport`, `recordIntakeChoice`.
- PRD R-4, R-5, R-6, HP-6 (stored report, byte-identical reads), UXQ-9 (choices editable after a run; apply to the next run); WP-5 (clean control: 0 errors, 0 warnings); R-5 counts (47 teaching days, 1 unit conflict, 1 malformed code, 3 non-existent codes, 2 bad filenames, 7 ELD mismatches).
- **Brief check:** serves the brief's requirement that the tool accept the unit-outline Google Sheet and show the author what it understood before generation; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given the issued sheet uploaded by NL-26's path, when any role GETs `/outline-versions/{id}/report`, then 200 with counts `teaching_days 47, unit_conflicts 1, malformed_codes 1, rows_with_nonexistent_code 3, bad_filenames 2, eld_mismatches 7` and `generate_allowed false` (WF-3) — verify: `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/[outlineVersionId]/report/route.test.ts::issued_sheet_counts` — evidence: response counts equal R-5's — covers: R-5, R-4, CON-3
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given WP-5 (clean control, SYN-3) uploaded, when the report is read, then every row `ok`, `errors 0`, `warnings 0`, `generate_allowed true` — verify: `report/route.test.ts::wp5_clean_control` — evidence: response and counts — covers: R-5, CON-3
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Given no choice recorded between two reads, when the report is read twice, then the two response bodies are byte-identical and the `model_call` table has zero rows (WF-3) — verify: `report/route.test.ts::reads_are_byte_identical_and_modelless` — evidence: equal bytes; row count 0 — covers: R-5, CON-G5, CON-3
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] Given runs started from this version, when the report is read, then `runs_from_this_version` lists them newest first with `choices_hash`, and is `[]` before the first run — verify: `report/route.test.ts::runs_from_this_version` — evidence: two responses — covers: CON-3
- [ ] AC-5 [failure/refusal] When the report is requested for an unknown version id, then 404 `NOT_FOUND`; reviewer and approver roles read 200 — verify: `report/route.test.ts::unknown_version_and_all_roles_read` — evidence: four responses — covers: CON-3, CON-G1
- [ ] AC-6 [negative] Given an outline cell containing `<script>alert(1)</script>` and a distinctive marker `ZQX-CELL-77`, when the report is read, then the markup appears only as escaped text in JSON strings and no response header or log line holds the marker (WF-3) — verify: `report/route.test.ts::cell_text_is_text_only` — evidence: response body and captured log scan — covers: CON-G6, R-58, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] Given an author confirms an error finding with `confirm_fix`, when the last unconfirmed error is confirmed, then the finding's `choice` is `{source: "confirmed", by: <author name>, at}`, `errors_unconfirmed` reaches 0, `generate_allowed` is true and `outline_version.confirmed_at` is set once (WF-3) — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::confirm_last_error_unlocks_generate` — evidence: response, `intake_choice` row, `outline_version.confirmed_at` — covers: R-5, CON-4, M-13
- [ ] AC-8 [invariant] Given one warning left untouched, when the report is read after the error was confirmed, then that warning's choice is `{source: "default"}` and no `intake_choice` row has status `confirmed` for it (WF-3) — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::untouched_warning_stays_default` — evidence: report and rows — covers: R-5, CON-4
- [ ] AC-9 [invariant] When `revert` is posted for a confirmed target, then the choice returns to its stored default and counts are restored; a second author's later write to the same target wins and both writes have an `audit_event` (CON-4) — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::revert_and_last_write_wins` — evidence: rows and two audit events — covers: CON-4, CON-G4
- [ ] AC-10 [failure/refusal] When a reviewer posts a choice, then 403 `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` and `intake_choice`, `audit_event` counts are unchanged — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::role_forbidden_writes_nothing` — evidence: response and unchanged counts — covers: CON-4, CON-G1, CON-G2, R-54
- [ ] AC-11 [failure/refusal] When `edit_fix` carries a code not in the seeded standards list (marker `ZZ.9.9`), then 422 `INVALID_CHOICE` with `details.reason` and no row is written; an unknown `target_id` gives 404 `NOT_FOUND` — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::invalid_choice_and_unknown_target` — evidence: two responses; unchanged counts — covers: CON-4, CON-G2
- [ ] AC-12 [failure/refusal] Given a run already started from the version, when `confirm_unit` names a different unit, then 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`; confirming a choice after the run started succeeds and the run's stored `choices_hash` is unchanged (UXQ-9) — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::late_unit_change_refused_choices_apply_next_run` — evidence: response; run row — covers: CON-4, R-16
- [ ] AC-13 [failure/refusal] When a foreign `Origin` header posts a choice, then 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` and no row is written — verify: `choices/route.test.ts::foreign_origin_refused` — evidence: response — covers: CON-G2, CON-1
- [ ] AC-14 [capture] Given the real handler, when `test_intake_confirm_capture` confirms one error and leaves one warning on default and then posts one refused choice, then it finds the two `intake_choice` rows, one `audit_event` naming the confirmer with the web `request_id` (WF-3), and the refusal wrote no row and left one log line with `request_id` and code — verify: `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/[outlineVersionId]/choices/route.test.ts::test_intake_confirm_capture` — evidence: rows, audit event, log line; no password or session token in any row — covers: OBS-1, OBS-3, OBS-7, M-13, CON-G4
- [ ] AC-15 [regression/context] area map row(s) for `apps/web/src/server/services/outline-service.ts` (report, record_choice), `apps/web/app/api/outline-versions/[outlineVersionId]/{report,choices}/route.ts` planned → actual (A4 intake service (DO-3 §2.3, §4)); router/ICM rows if a route's evidence changed; dev-log entry (Changed · Why · Checked · Remaining); the slice plan's wiring-owner row ticked where this ticket fills one — verify: `git diff --stat` and `python3 ~/.claude/skills/icm-project/scripts/check_context.py .` — evidence: diff touches only those rows; no FAIL — covers: OBS-11

US-7 — As an author I watch the lessons being written (one tile per lesson with running cost) so I can see the run is healthy. US-8 — I recover from failures without paying twice (cancel, retry failed, resume). US-9 — I read the unit plan first. US-32 — I read the run summary (cost, retries, failures, calls lost, brakes fired).

### What to build
Add four methods to the `RunService` NL-27 created (`start` is NL-27's; **same file, methods plus wiring**) and fill the web wiring file `wire_runs` (DO-4 §12) so `services.runs` is a real object:

- `progress(user, run_id) -> RunProgress` (CON-6): one indexed read of the run's `lesson_job` rows (≤ 47) plus the run row; per tile `tile_state(job)` (DO-4 §8 *lifecycle*), `attempts`, `repair_used`, `truncation_retry_used`, `failure_reasons` (the OpenAPI `FailureReason.check` vocabulary), `cost_usd`, `openable` (true only for `ready`); run-level `state`, `paused_reason`, `capped_by` (`RunRow.capped_by`, same three values as CON-6, no mapping), `spent_usd`, `reserved_usd`, `cap_usd`, `concurrency_cap` (`GENERATION_CONCURRENCY`), `queued_ahead`, `counts_by_tile_state`, `updated_at`.
- `plan(user, run_id) -> UnitPlan` (CON-8): `UnitPlanRow` + the run's copied `lesson_links`; `state` `planning | stored | failed`.
- `control(user, run_id, req) -> RunControlResult` (CON-7): role `author`; in one tx `RunRepo.lock_for_update` (the row lock that stops two clicks both applying) → `decide_run_control(current, action)` (`INVALID_TRANSITION` with `details.state`) → `JobQueue.requeue_failed` / `JobQueue.cancel_run(run_id, "cancelled")` / resume (re-queues a failed plan, `RunRepo.set_state`) → one `audit_event`. NOTIFY `lesson_job` after commit when jobs were requeued.
- `summary(user, run_id) -> RunSummary` (CON-21): totals from `ModelCallLog.totals_for_run` and `RunRepo.summary_rows`; `cost_per_ready_lesson_usd` = total cost ÷ ready lessons (empty when none), `calls_lost_in_flight`, `brakes_fired`, `truncation_retries`, `p95_minutes_per_lesson`, `target_minutes_per_lesson 5`, `report_path`; a mismatch between run spend and call sums sets the *trace incomplete* flag (DO-6 completeness check 1).
- Routes under `apps/web/app/api/runs/[runId]/` (`progress` GET, `plan` GET, `actions` POST, `summary` GET) through `with_route`; `apps/web/src/server/wiring/runs.ts` builds `RunService` from `WebDeps` with `PgRunRepo`, `PgJobQueue`, `PgOutlineRepo`, `PgLessonRepo`, `PgPromptRepo`, `PgSpendLedger`, `PgModelCallLog`, `PgAuditLog`, `TxRunner` (all earlier-wave real objects) and `RunWiring.runs`.

**Must not:** stream (progress is polled, shared guarantee 9); recompute spend from anything but stored rows; add a "raise the cap" action (UXP-5); write any row on a read or on a refusal.

### Story
US-7 — As an author (P-2) I need to watch lessons being written and open the finished ones; US-8 — I need a killed or failed run to carry on without paying twice. This ticket is the join that makes both true: it wires every generation piece built so far into one running worker and proves, on the stub provider, that a queued run really becomes stored lessons.

### What to build
- `apps/worker/src/wiring/generation.ts` (A0 created the shell in NL-07; this ticket is its only filler): implement `wire_generation(d: WorkerDeps) -> GenerationWiring` (DO-4 §12 composition roots) so `GenerationWiring.claim_loop` is a real `ClaimLoop` (DO-4 §6) built from concrete parts, in this order: `PgJobQueue` (NL-28) · `ModelCallRecorder` over `d.model_client` + `PgModelCallLog` (NL-33) · `PriceTable` · `PgSpendLedger` (NL-35, constructed with `PgRepo_ctor{db, ids, clock}`) · `PaidCaller(recorder, spend, prices)` · the prompt renderer (NL-14) with the pinned prompt row (NL-34) · `DraftNode`, `CompileCheckNode`, `RepairNode`, `StoreNode`, `FailNode` (NL-29; the store node writes through the NL-36 document-store port, never a direct `lesson_doc` insert) · `UnitPlanJob` (NL-31) · `RunFinalizer` (NL-30) · `LessonJobRunner` · `ClaimLoop`. `d.model_client` is already the stub or the Anthropic adapter, chosen by `MODEL_PROVIDER_MODE` in `apps/worker/src/main.ts` (A0); this file never reads the mode and never imports an SDK (`packages/llm` is the only importer, boundaries lint).
- Tests (this ticket writes them): `apps/worker/src/wiring/generation.int.test.ts` on the repo's Postgres test-container helper (NL-08), with `StubModelClient` (`packages/llm/src/stub.ts`) scripted from synthetic fixtures `apps/worker/test/fixtures/stub-drafts/wp-1.json` and `wp-2.json` (hand-derived from the *Required output* of WP-1 and WP-2 in `docs/data/worked-pairs.md`; each fixture names its source in a header field, per `.claude/rules/synthetic-test-data.md`). The tests start a run through `RunService.start` (NL-27) and let the **real** `ClaimLoop.run_until` claim; no job is called by hand.
- Must not: edit `apps/worker/src/main.ts`, `wiring/checks.ts`, `wiring/judge.ts` or any package from NL-14…NL-43 (a defect found there goes back as a fix ticket, not an edit here); call a real provider; store or log a provider key; add a dependency (A0).

## [NL-80] collab: Hocuspocus server — socket auth from the app session, per-update write guard with `refused`/`refused_from`, debounced persistence, `stored`/`mode` acks; fills collab server wiring

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-15 — As a reviewer I edit together with a colleague and know my time is counted fairly, so that two of us can finish a lesson together without losing each other's work. Platform: this is the only process that writes lesson content (R-26), and the one that refuses typing after Submit.

### What to build
Build the Hocuspocus server's behaviour (the socket on `lesson:<lesson_id>`, CON-12). The internal command routes and the Submit freeze are NL-105 and NL-106; `main.ts` and `health.ts` are NL-07 / NL-83.

- `frozen-docs.ts` — `FrozenDocs` (in memory, one process, PD-9): `is_frozen`, `freeze`, `unfreeze`, `seed(lesson_id, state)` (frozen unless `is_editable(state, "reviewer")`).
- `auth.ts` — `CollabAuthenticator.authenticate(SocketAuthRequest)`: reads the `ls_session` cookie (`SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`) from the upgrade request, `SessionRepo.resolve`; expired, revoked or unknown → `DomainRefusal(UNAUTHENTICATED)` and the connection is refused before the document loads; loads the lesson's state, builds `SocketContext{user, lesson_id, lesson_state, read_only}` from `WriteGuard.can_write`, seeds `FrozenDocs` on the document's first connection.
- `permissions.ts` — `WriteGuard.can_write(role, state, lesson_id)` at connect (read-only unless `is_editable(state, role)` and not frozen; **only `reviewer` connections write**, authors and approvers read) and `WriteGuard.on_update(ctx, frozen)` per message from Hocuspocus `beforeHandleMessage`: a frozen document or a read-only connection is refused **before the update is applied**; the caller sends `AckBroadcaster.refused(socket_id, LESSON_LOCKED, message, refused_from)` with the client's state vector before the refused update, then drops the update (SP-2 option A).
- `persistence.ts` — `LessonPersistence.load` (latest `lesson_doc`; an unknown `schema_version` fails loudly with the lesson id) and `store` (`onStoreDocument` after `STORE_DEBOUNCE_MS` 2000, max `STORE_MAX_DEBOUNCE_MS` 4000): `ydoc_to_lesson` → `content_hash` → `LessonDocStore.store` in **one transaction** (Y.Doc bytes, derived JSON, hash, state vector, coalesced `check_job`, last editor, audit; mints `store_id`) → `AckBroadcaster.stored`.
- `acks.ts` — `AckBroadcaster`: stateless messages `{type:"stored", content_hash, state_vector, stored_at}`, `{type:"mode", mode, state}`, `{type:"refused", code, message, refused_from}` exactly as CON-12's `x-collaboration-channel`.
- `wiring/server.ts` — fills the server half of the collab composition (auth, guard, frozen set, persistence, acks) from `CollabDeps` with `PgSessionRepo`, `PgLessonRepo`, `PgLessonDocStore`, `PgLessonDocReader`, `PgAuditLog` (the command-handler half is `wiring/commands.ts`, NL-105).

**Must not:** accept a write from a non-reviewer, an unauthenticated or a frozen document; persist an edit that was refused; start a model client or require a provider key (Metz S4); log cookies, tokens or lesson text; close connections to enforce the freeze (SP-2 rejected option B).

### Sources
- DO-4 §7 (all classes above), §3.4 `LessonDocStore`, `LessonDocReader`, §3.5 `SessionRepo`, `LessonStateRepo`, §8 *ydoc* (`ydoc_to_lesson`, `content_hash`), *lifecycle* (`is_editable`), §9 `CollabSettings`; DO-3 §2.5, §5 (SP-2 decision), §7 (`STORE_DEBOUNCE_MS`).
- CON-12 (agreed); OpenAPI `x-collaboration-channel`; SP-2 record `docs/analysis/spikes/SP-2-freeze-at-submit.md` (option A, refused keystrokes, 20-trial assertions, round-trip hash).
- PRD R-26, R-33, R-54, HP-4, HP-5; PD-9; WP-1.
- **Brief check:** serves "collaborative … editor … session-authenticated, persisted within 2 s, only the collaboration server writes lesson content"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [failure/refusal] Given an upgrade request with no cookie, an unknown token, an expired session or a revoked session, when it connects to `lesson:<id>`, then the connection is refused with `UNAUTHENTICATED`, the document is never loaded and no `lesson_doc` row is touched (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/auth.test.ts::unauthenticated_refused_before_load` — evidence: four refusals; load spy 0 calls — covers: R-26, R-54, CON-12, CON-G1
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given a signed-in author, approver and reviewer on an `in_review` lesson, then author and approver connect `read_only`, the reviewer connects writable; on `draft`, `submitted`, `approved`, `exported` every role is read-only (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/permissions.test.ts::role_and_state_matrix` — evidence: 12-cell matrix — covers: R-33, R-54, CON-12
- [ ] AC-3 [failure/refusal] Given a reviewer socket on a writable lesson and `FrozenDocs.freeze(id)` called, when the client sends an update, then the update is refused before it is applied: the server document's state vector is unchanged, no `lesson_doc` row is written, and that socket alone receives `{type:"refused", code:"LESSON_LOCKED", refused_from: <its state vector before the update>}` (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/persistence.int.test.ts::frozen_update_refused_not_applied` — evidence: message; vector equality; row count — covers: R-33, HP-5, CON-12, CON-G2
- [ ] AC-4 [failure/refusal] Given a read-only (author) connection that sends an update, then it is refused with `LESSON_LOCKED` the same way and the co-editors receive nothing (WF-9) — verify: `persistence.int.test.ts::read_only_connection_update_refused` — evidence: refused message; other clients' log empty — covers: R-54, CON-12
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] Given two real provider clients editing the same lesson with 20 edits inside 2 s, then one store occurs after the debounce (and none later than `STORE_MAX_DEBOUNCE_MS`), exactly one new `lesson_doc` row with `content_hash`, `state_vector` and a `check_job` for that hash, and both clients receive one `stored` message with the same hash (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/persistence.int.test.ts::test_store_capture` — evidence: rows; messages — covers: R-26, R-28, CON-12, M-26
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] The stored row's last editor is the user whose update was last stored; after a restart `load` returns the stored document and storing it unchanged yields the same `content_hash` (round trip) (WF-9) — verify: `persistence.int.test.ts::last_editor_and_roundtrip_hash` — evidence: ids; hash equality — covers: R-26, HP-4, M-36, M-8
- [ ] AC-7 [failure/refusal] Given a stored document with an unknown `schema_version` (99), when it loads, then the load fails with an error naming the lesson id and no document is served — verify: `persistence.test.ts::unknown_schema_version_fails_loudly` — evidence: thrown error — covers: R-11, R-58
- [ ] AC-8 [invariant] On connect to a frozen state the server seeds `FrozenDocs` from `lesson.state` (frozen unless editable for a reviewer) and sends `mode` with the lesson state; after `unfreeze` followed by `AckBroadcaster.mode(editable)` the reviewer can write again (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/frozen-docs.test.ts::seed_on_first_connection_and_mode_message` — evidence: state flags; messages — covers: R-33, CON-12
- [ ] AC-9 [invariant] Store transaction time at p95 over 50 stores with a 47-lesson-sized document is at most 500 ms, and a failed store transaction leaves no partial `lesson_doc` / `check_job` / `audit_event` rows and no `stored` message (WF-9) — verify: `persistence.int.test.ts::store_tx_p95_and_atomicity` — evidence: measured p95; row counts — covers: HP-4, M-27, CON-12
- [ ] AC-10 [negative] When a session cookie value, a distinctive lesson sentence (`COLLAB-QZ-80`) and a provider-key marker pass through connect, edit and refuse, then none appears in any log line, ack message to other clients, or table other than the stored lesson content (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/auth.test.ts::no_cookie_text_or_key_in_logs` — evidence: scan zero matches — covers: OBS-7, GR-9
- [ ] AC-11 [invariant] The collab process starts with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` unset and `CollabSettings` parses without them — verify: `apps/collab/src/wiring/server.test.ts::starts_without_provider_keys` — evidence: process starts; no model import in the bundle (grep) — covers: GR-13, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-12 [capture] Given two scripted real Hocuspocus provider clients, when `test_store_capture` also freezes the lesson and a client keeps typing, then it asserts one `lesson_doc` per store with hash and state vector, a `check_job` for the new hash, and that the post-freeze write got a `refused` message and wrote no `lesson_doc` or `audit_event` row (one application-log line with the `lesson_id`) (WF-9) — verify: `apps/collab/src/persistence.int.test.ts::test_store_capture` and `apps/collab/src/wiring/server.test.ts::wire_server_builds_all_parts` — evidence: rows, message, log line — covers: OBS-1, OBS-4, M-19, M-24, M-26, M-36
- [ ] AC-13 [regression/context] area map row(s) for `apps/collab/src/{auth,permissions,persistence,acks,frozen-docs}.ts`, `apps/collab/src/wiring/server.ts` planned → actual (A11 collab server (DO-3 §2.5, §4)); router/ICM rows if a route's evidence changed; dev-log entry (Changed · Why · Checked · Remaining); the slice plan's wiring-owner row ticked where this ticket fills one — verify: `git diff --stat` and `python3 ~/.claude/skills/icm-project/scripts/check_context.py .` — evidence: diff touches only those rows; no FAIL — covers: OBS-11

## [NL-81] checks: check job runner in its own worker lane (issues, alignment links, dependants re-queued); fills checks wiring

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-16/US-17/US-20 (with US-14, US-18, US-24, US-25) — As a reviewer I see a new blocking issue within seconds of an edit, so that what blocks Submit and Approve is always current. Platform: after every durable store, the deterministic suite runs in its own worker lane so checks never wait behind generation.

### What to build
Build the after-store check lane and fill its wiring.

- `apps/worker/src/checks/check-job-runner.ts` — `CheckJobRunner.run_once() -> CheckRunReport | null` (DO-4 §6): `CheckQueue.claim(lease_ms)` → `LessonDocReader.latest_derived` (the **stored derived row**, never the live Y.Doc; skip and `finish` if a newer hash is already queued) → `CheckContextLoader.load` → `run_checks(CHECK_RULES, CHECK_POLICY)` (NL-20/38/39/40/41) → in one `TxRunner.with_tx`: `IssueRepo.replace_for_hash` (carries resolutions to an identical finding; the rest `cleared_by "fix"`) + `AlignmentRepo.replace_for_hash` for that hash → `CheckQueue.finish` → `LessonGraphRepo.dependants(lesson_id)` and `CheckQueue.enqueue` for each dependant whose `cross_lesson_link` result may change. Returns `CheckRunReport{blocking, confirmation, advisory, dependants_requeued, duration_ms}`.
- The loop that calls it: polls every `CHECK_POLL_MS` (500), claims from its **own lane — independent of the generation semaphore** (`GENERATION_CONCURRENCY`), renews/expires leases like the generation lane, and on SIGTERM stops claiming and finishes the check in hand.
- `apps/worker/src/wiring/checks.ts` — `wire_checks` fills `CheckWiring{check_runner}` from `WorkerDeps` with `PgCheckQueue`, `PgLessonDocReader`, `PgIssueRepo`, `PgAlignmentRepo`, `PgLessonGraphRepo`, `CheckContextLoader`, `CHECK_RULES`, `CHECK_POLICY`, `TxRunner`.

**Must not:** call a model (checks are deterministic: zero `model_call` rows); write a partial issue set (one tx); write content; block on or share a slot with generation; edit rule modules (NL-20/39/40/41), `CheckPolicy` values or `CHECK_RULES`.

### Sources
- DO-4 §6 `CheckJobRunner`, `CheckRunReport`, `CheckContextLoader`, `CheckContext`, §3.5 `CheckQueue`, `IssueRepo`, `AlignmentRepo`, `LessonGraphRepo`, `LessonDocReader`, §8 *checks*, §12 `wire_checks`; DO-3 §2.4, §6 (`check_job`, `issue`, `alignment_link`), §7 (`CHECK_POLL_MS`).
- CON-13 (agreed; `pending`, `checked_hash`, timing ≤ 5 s); INTERFACE *Timing*; DO-1 D-6 (coalesced `check_job`, own lane).
- PRD R-19, R-20, R-28, R-34; HP-3; SP-3 (name scan blocking in `cfu_item`s only); WP-1.
- **Brief check:** serves "checks re-run on every durable save, reading the stored derived row"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given a stored edit that deletes a lesson's only checking item, when the check lane runs, then a blocking `issue` exists for the new `content_hash`, `pending` clears, and `checked_at` is within 5,000 ms of the store (WF-10) — verify: `apps/worker/src/checks/check-job-runner.int.test.ts::test_checks_after_store_capture` — evidence: issue row, `CheckQueue.pending_for` result, timing — covers: R-19, R-28, M-26, CON-13
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] With all `GENERATION_CONCURRENCY` slots held by blocked stub jobs, a queued `check_job` is still claimed and finished within 2,000 ms (own lane) (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::not_blocked_by_generation_slots` — evidence: finish time; slot count 6/6 busy — covers: R-28, CON-13, M-26
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Two stores in quick succession (hashes H1, H2) coalesce to one queued row; when H1 is claimed and H2 is already queued, the runner skips H1 without writing issues and checks H2 (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::coalesced_newer_hash_wins` — evidence: issue rows keyed only to H2 — covers: R-28, CON-13
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] The issue and alignment replacement for a hash is one transaction: a rule that throws leaves no partial `issue` / `alignment_link` rows, logs `lesson_id`, `content_hash` and the rule name (no lesson text), releases the claim and lets the next lesson proceed (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::rule_throw_rolls_back_and_continues` — evidence: row counts; log line — covers: R-19, OBS-8
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] Given a resolution recorded on H1 for a finding that is identical on H2 (same kind, address, code), then the H2 issue carries the resolution; a finding that disappears is `cleared_by "fix"` (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::resolutions_carry_forward` — evidence: issue rows — covers: R-34, CON-13
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] Given Lesson 4 links to Lesson 5's slot, when Lesson 5 is stored, then Lesson 4 gets a queued check and `CheckRunReport.dependants_requeued >= 1`; a lesson without dependants requeues none (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::dependants_requeued` — evidence: queue rows; report — covers: R-28, R-34, CON-13
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] Given the same hash checked twice, the issue set is identical (idempotent), and no `model_call` row exists after a run of 20 checks (WF-10) — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::idempotent_and_modelless` — evidence: equal issue sets; call count 0 — covers: R-19, GR-12
- [ ] AC-8 [failure/refusal] Given a claim whose lease expired (worker killed mid-check), when the lane polls, then another claim finishes it once and no duplicate issue set exists — verify: `check-job-runner.int.test.ts::expired_lease_reclaimed` — evidence: queue row; issue rows — covers: R-28, OBS-8

## [NL-82] ops: seed CDE standards, prompt v1, one demo account per role

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-37 — As a staff member I sign in and see only what my role can do, so that only an author starts a run and only an approver approves. Platform: the demo needs the official standards tables, the first prompt version and one account per role to exist on a fresh database (R-4, R-54).

### What to build
Write `ops/seed.ts`: `seed_reference_data(db: PgDatabase) -> SeedReport{standards, users, ops_event_id}` (DO-4 §11) and its `npm run db:seed` entry. Idempotent: running it twice leaves the same rows.

- **Standards (R-4, GR-5):** loads the official CDE tables prepared by NL-15 under `packages/core/data/standards/**` (CCSS ELA 6, ELD 6, MSLS 6) into `standard` (`code`, `set`, `text`, `parent_code`, `is_leaf`, `eld_strand`) through `PgStandardRepo`. It reads those files; it does not re-author them and never reads `docs/source/restricted/`.
- **Prompt v1:** inserts `prompt_version` number 1 (locked layer hash from `packages/prompts`, empty guidance) via `PgPromptRepo`/NL-34's seed function, once.
- **Demo accounts:** exactly one account per role (`author`, `reviewer`, `approver`) in `app_user` with `synthetic = true` (set only here; no API route can set it), emails on the allow list, and `password_hash` from `hash_password` imported from **`packages/core/src/auth/passwords.ts`** (scrypt via `node:crypto`; the orchestrator moved it there so the seed and the web app share one hasher without breaking dependency arrows; slice plan open item 2 is closed that way). The plaintext password comes from the `SEED_DEMO_PASSWORD` environment variable; if it is unset the script generates a 20-character random password and writes it **only** to the git-ignored `.demo/seed-credentials.txt` (mode 600), never to stdout, logs, `ops_event` or any table. Nothing in the repository holds a password.
- One `ops_event` (`kind "seed"`, counts per standard set, never a password or hash) via `EvidenceRepo.ops_event`.

**Must not:** import from `apps/web` (dependency arrows); commit credentials; create more than one account per role; mark a non-seed user `synthetic`; load anything that is not CDE standards text.

### Sources
- DO-4 §9/§11 (`seed_reference_data`, `SeedReport`), §3.5 `StandardRepo`, `PromptRepo`, `SessionRepo`, `EvidenceRepo.ops_event`; DO-3 §2.6 (`ops/seed.ts`), §6 (`app_user`, `standard`, `prompt_version`, `ops_event`).
- CON-1 (card text: one account per role, scrypt password hashes, `synthetic` seed-only; the sign-in route is NL-25); INTERFACE shared guarantee 1.
- PRD R-4, R-54, GR-5, GR-13; PD-25 (HP-8 amendment: reviewer and approver accounts, Claude-driven accounts synthetic); DO-6 WF-37.
- **Brief check:** serves "seeded official CDE standards tables" and "one demo account per role"; touches nothing out of scope (no student or teacher-of-record data, GR-13); weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given an empty migrated database, when `seed_reference_data` runs, then `standard` holds the expected counts per set (CCSS ELA 6, ELD 6, MSLS 6 as prepared by NL-15), `prompt_version` has number 1 exactly once, `app_user` has exactly three rows (one per role) and one `ops_event` of kind `seed` exists (WF-37) — verify: `ops/seed.test.ts::test_seed_counts` — evidence: row counts equal NL-15's manifest counts — covers: R-4, R-54, GR-5, OBS-9
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] When the seed runs twice, then row counts are unchanged and the second `ops_event` records `0` new rows (idempotent) (WF-37) — verify: `ops/seed.test.ts::seed_is_idempotent` — evidence: counts before/after — covers: R-4, OBS-9
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Each demo account signs in through the real `POST /session` handler (NL-25) with the seeded password and gets its own role; `synthetic` is true for all seed accounts, and no route changes it (WF-37) — verify: `ops/seed.int.test.ts::seeded_accounts_sign_in_with_their_role` — evidence: three sessions with roles author, reviewer, approver — covers: R-54, CON-1, CON-G1
- [ ] AC-4 [negative] After a seed run with `SEED_DEMO_PASSWORD=<test-seed-password>` the plaintext appears in no table, no `ops_event.details_json`, no stdout / log capture and no tracked file; `password_hash` is a scrypt string (WF-37) — verify: `ops/seed.test.ts::password_never_stored_or_logged` — evidence: scan zero matches; hash prefix check — covers: OBS-7, R-54, GR-13
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] With `SEED_DEMO_PASSWORD` unset the script generates a 20-character password, writes it only to `.demo/seed-credentials.txt` with mode 600 and that path is git-ignored (`git check-ignore`), and the seed still reports success (WF-37) — verify: `ops/seed.test.ts::generated_password_only_in_ignored_file` — evidence: file mode, check-ignore exit 0, scan of stdout — covers: OBS-7
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] `ops/seed.ts` imports `hash_password` from `packages/core/src/auth/passwords.ts` and nothing from `apps/web`; the boundaries lint (NL-01) passes — verify: `npm run lint -- ops/seed.ts` and `ops/seed.test.ts::no_web_import` — evidence: lint exit 0 — covers: R-54

- [ ] AC-11 [coverage] driving WF-37's real entry point, each obligation below holds in that workflow — GR-5: Cite only official SBE standards text from the CDE, never the sheet's labels; GR-9: Crawled Newsela content stays in git-ignored docs/source/restricted/; never comm; GR-13: No student or teacher-of-record data; staff authentication only; OBS-11: A new entry point, job, script or experiment registers its WF-n row, inherited s — verify: `wf-37-obligations` test file in this ticket's owned test folder, one case per id, run against the real stack — evidence: test output listing every id as passed — covers: GR-5, GR-9, GR-13, OBS-11
- [ ] AC-10 [regression/context] area map row(s) for `ops/seed.ts` (`npm run db:seed`), `ops/seed.test.ts` planned → actual (A21 ops (DO-3 §2.6, §4)); router/ICM rows if a route's evidence changed; dev-log entry (Changed · Why · Checked · Remaining); the slice plan's wiring-owner row ticked where this ticket fills one — verify: `git diff --stat` and `python3 ~/.claude/skills/icm-project/scripts/check_context.py .` — evidence: diff touches only those rows; no FAIL — covers: OBS-11

## [NL-83] ops: health routes on web/worker/collab, process start events, backup script, sample-builder event

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Platform ticket (no user story): the deploy and the recording need liveness probes, an auditable start of every process, a verified database backup after the full run (PD-30) and a logged sample build. It serves US-36 (trust the build's numbers) indirectly: the backup is what protects the full-run evidence.

### What to build
Fill the operations surface NL-07 stubbed.

- **Health (WF-39):** `GET /healthz` on each process. `apps/worker/src/health.ts`: `serve_health(db, port, service) -> HealthServer`; `apps/collab/src/health.ts`: same through Hocuspocus `onRequest`; `apps/web/app/api/healthz/route.ts` (no `with_route` session; open, liveness only). Response `200 {"status":"ok","service","build_id"}` when `PgDatabase.ping` succeeds, else `503 {"status":"unavailable","service"}` plus one `ops_event` of kind `health.failure` (at most one per 60 s per process; if the event write also fails the 503 still returns and the failure goes to the JSON log; the handler never throws). The body carries no connection string, no env value and no version of anything else.
- **Start events (WF-38):** every process writes one `ops_event` `process.start` with `service` and a non-empty `build_id` (`BUILD_ID` = `RENDER_GIT_COMMIT` or the local git SHA). Web: `apps/web/instrumentation.ts` (Next `register`); worker and collab: the call NL-07 left in `main.ts`; if it is missing NL-83 may add that single call (the one allowed edit to NL-07 files, noted in the review).
- **Backup (WF-40):** `ops/backup.sh` (`npm run ops:backup`): one `pg_dump` in custom format to a git-ignored `backups/` path with mode 600; records one `ops_event` `backup` with path, size and SHA-256; verifies it with `pg_restore --list`. The database password is passed through the environment, never argv; the script refuses to run without `DATABASE_URL`.
- **Sample builder (WF-35):** `ops/run-sample-builder.ts` runs `docs/data/scripts/build_samples.py` and records one `ops_event` `samples.built` with the hashes of its inputs and outputs.

**Must not:** publish Postgres or expose the backup path over HTTP; put a secret in a health body, event, argv or log; call a model; change the build script.

### Sources
- DO-4 §3.5 `EvidenceRepo.ops_event`, `OpsEventRecord`, §6 `HealthServer`, `serve_health`, §9 `build_id`; DO-3 §2.4–§2.6, §6 (`ops_event`), §7 (`BUILD_ID`).
- DO-6 WF-35, WF-38, WF-39, WF-40 (capture tests named below); OBS-9, OBS-10; slice plan *Composition-root wiring owners* (health row).
- PRD §8 guardrails; PD-30 (backup after the full run, before recording).
- **Brief check:** serves the brief's deployable, demonstrable prototype requirement (a running app that can be probed and recovered); touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given Postgres reachable, when `GET /healthz` is called on web, worker and collab, then each returns 200 with `status ok`, its `service` and a non-empty `build_id`, and writes no `ops_event` (WF-39) — verify: `apps/web/app/api/healthz/route.test.ts::ok_when_postgres_reachable` and the worker / collab `health.test.ts` equivalents — evidence: three 200 bodies; event count 0 — covers: OBS-9, OBS-8
- [ ] AC-2 [failure/refusal] Given `PgDatabase.ping` failing, when `GET /healthz` is called, then 503 `unavailable`, exactly one `ops_event` `health.failure` for that service, and a second call within 60 s writes no second event; when the event write also fails the 503 still returns and one JSON log line records it (WF-39) — verify: `health.test.ts::test_healthz` — evidence: status, events, log line — covers: OBS-9, OBS-8
- [ ] AC-3 [negative] With `DATABASE_URL` containing the password marker `QzDb-Pass-83` and a provider-key marker set, no health body, `ops_event` row, log line or start event contains either (WF-39, WF-38) — verify: `health.test.ts::no_secrets_in_health_or_events` — evidence: scan zero matches — covers: OBS-7, OBS-9
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] When each of the three processes starts against a test database, then one `ops_event` `process.start` exists per process with its `service` and a non-empty `build_id` equal to `BUILD_ID` or the git SHA (WF-38) — verify: `ops/start-events.int.test.ts::test_start_event` — evidence: three events — covers: OBS-9, GR-14
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] Given a test database, when `ops/backup.sh` runs, then one dump file exists under the git-ignored `backups/` path with mode 600, `pg_restore --list` reads it, and one `ops_event` `backup` records path, size and a SHA-256 equal to `sha256sum` of the file (WF-40) — verify: `ops/backup.test.ts::test_backup_logs_event` — evidence: file, listing, event — covers: OBS-9, OBS-8

### Story
US-3 — As an author I see every problem in the outline before any money is spent. US-36 — As the builder I trust the numbers before the demo: the intake and safety golden suites run in the merge gate and prove the deterministic layer is right before any model is paid.

### What to build
Fill the two suite shells NL-49 created (`evals/src/suites/s1.ts`, `s7.ts`, each an `EvalSuite`, DO-4 §11) and add their cases. Both are **deterministic and model-free**; `EvalRunner` (NL-49) writes one `eval_case_result` per case and the report.

- **S1 intake golden** (`npm run eval:golden -- --suite intake`): for each case the normalizer, code resolver and `build_validation_report` (NL-15/16/17) run on the case input and the **expected fields** are compared exactly. Cases: the issued sheet (`docs/data/samples/g6-u4-lesson-outline.json` and the issued row samples; expected counts 47 teaching days, 1 unit conflict, 1 malformed code, 3 non-existent codes, 2 bad filenames, 7 ELD mismatches), SYN-2 (layout-shifted sheet, `synthetic-2026-10-24-syn2-layout-shifted.csv`), WP-5 (clean control: 0 errors, 0 warnings) and **one test per outline defect** (R-51 part 1). Two runs must be byte-identical; the suite also asserts no `model_call` row exists after it ran (HP-6).
- **S7 safety notes** (`npm run eval:golden -- --suite safety`): WP-4 four checks (the row-39 content warning is **proposed** as a safety note, **routed** to the teacher-only tip, **absent** from every student-facing block, and **Approve refused** until a named person clears the flag: via `run_checks` + `approve_gate` on the fixture lesson, no route needed); recall over the SYN-4+ planted warnings and decoys written by `docs/data/scripts/build_samples.py` or its successor (labelled synthetic, with *n*); false proposals over the issued sheet's 620 cells (≤ 1) and over WP-5 (0); every cleared flag carries user, note and time.
- Cases live under `evals/cases/s1/**` and `evals/cases/s7/**`, each with `provenance` (`issued`, `hand-written`, `synthetic`), `source`, `guards` (DO-5 *Case provenance*); expected values come from the authority in DO-5 (hand-counted sheet, HP-6, HP-9), never from the output being tested.

**Must not:** call a model; derive an expected value by running the code under test; use `docs/source/restricted/`; change intake or check code (a failing case is reported to its owning ticket).

### Sources

## [NL-86] evals: full-run driver over the OpenAPI (Prism-tested) and S9/S13 report builder from stored rows

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — As the builder I trust the build's numbers before the demo: a full 47-day run of the issued unit, driven through the product's own HTTP API, with a report whose every number is read from stored rows (R-51), so the video never states a number the database cannot back.

### What to build
Build the machinery for the one real full run (NL-112 runs it; this ticket proves it on the stub and the Prism mock).

- `evals/src/driver/**` — an HTTP driver over the OpenAPI (`docs/contracts/interface.openapi.yaml`, generated types from NL-11): `signIn` (credentials from `DRIVER_EMAIL` / `DRIVER_PASSWORD`, never stored or logged), `uploadOutline`, `getValidationReport`, `recordIntakeChoice` (confirm each error with `confirm_fix`), `startRun` (with an `Idempotency-Key`), poll `getRunProgress` every 2 s until terminal, `getRunSummary`. It calls **only** the public API (no database writes, no service imports). In real provider mode it refuses to start unless `--cap-usd` is given and is at most `BUILD_SPEND_CEILING_USD`.
- `evals/src/full-run-report.ts` — `build_full_run_report(run_id) -> FullRunReport` (DO-4 §11): *n*, `first_pass_schema_valid`, `repairs`, `failures_by_reason`, `placeholders`, `grounding_flags_by_kind`, `confirmations` (median per lesson), `cost_usd`, `report_path`, built **only from stored rows** (`RunRepo.summary_rows`, `ModelCallLog.totals_for_run`, `IssueRepo`, `AlignmentRepo`, `lesson_version` hashes). Writes `evals/reports/full-run-<run_id>.md` and stores the path on the `eval_run` row.
- `evals/src/suites/s9.ts` (`npm run eval:full-run -- --unit G6-U4`) and `s13.ts` (draft quality: every approved lesson rated, rating split with *n* from the frozen `lesson_metrics` rows; ≥ 2 of 3 demo lessons `usable_with_edits` or better): fill the NL-49 shells; thresholds from DO-5 (S9: first-pass schema-valid ≥ 90%, 100% terminal with reasons, round-trip hash 47/47, spend ≤ run cap, ≤ $1 per lesson, p95 ≤ 5 min, wall ≤ 2 h, summary totals equal call sums).

**Must not:** spend real money in any test (stub provider; the Prism mock for the driver's contract test); write to the database outside the public API; embed a credential; invent a number not present in a stored row.

### Sources
- DO-4 §11 `FullRunReport`, `build_full_run_report`, `EvalSuite`, `EvalRunner`; DO-5 `eval-plan.md` S9 and S13 rows (*Acceptance conditions*, *Verification and evidence*); DO-6 WF-25 (`test_full_run_report_shape`).
- CON-2, CON-3, CON-4, CON-5, CON-21 (the operations driven); OpenAPI examples; `docs/contracts/generated/api-types.ts`.
- PRD R-51, R-55, GR-14 (demo honesty: numbers from stored rows); PD-29 (build spend ceiling); WP-1…WP-3.
- **Brief check:** serves "a full run of the issued unit with its report before recording" (R-51) and honest numbers (GR-14); touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria

## [NL-87] evals: spike report importer (SP-1…SP-3)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Platform ticket (no user story): the three spikes (SP-1 one-call draft, SP-2 freeze at Submit, SP-3 invention scans) ran before the database existed. Their results must land in `experiment_run` and `model_call` once it does, so build spend (M-29) and the spike evidence are queryable like any other record (R-48).

### What to build
Write `ops/import-spike.ts`: `import_spike_report(path: str) -> ImportReport{experiment_id, model_calls_imported}` (DO-4 §11) and the CLI `npm run ops:import-spike -- <report>`.

- Input: a spike report: the committed record `docs/analysis/spikes/SP-N-*.md` (its result tables) plus, for SP-1, the run ledger / per-call results exported from branch `spike/SP-1` (`git show spike/SP-1:spikes/sp1/...`). The importer parses the result tables into one `ExperimentRunRecord` (`experiment_id` `SP-1`/`SP-2`/`SP-3` plus a run suffix, `config`, `result`, `report_path`) via `EvidenceRepo.insert_experiment_run`, and for each recorded model call one `model_call` row (`purpose "spike"`, `experiment_id` set, tokens, `cost_usd`, `stop_reason`, `served_model`, no `run_id`) via `ModelCallLog`/`ModelCallStart` + `complete`, so M-29 (build spend against the ceiling) includes spike spend (G-5).
- **Idempotent:** keyed by `experiment_id` + call id; importing the same report twice writes nothing new.
- Fixtures under `evals/tests/fixtures/spike/` are trimmed copies of the three records (synthetic-free: they hold only the published result tables, no model output text beyond what the records already print).

**Must not:** call a model; invent a call that the report does not record; import prompt or output text from restricted content (GR-9); edit the spike records or branches.

### Sources
- DO-4 §11 `ImportReport`, `import_spike_report`, `ExperimentRunRecord`, §3.4 `ModelCallLog`, `ModelCallStart` (`purpose "spike"`, `experiment_id`), `EvidenceRepo`; DO-3 §2.6, §6 (`experiment_run`, `model_call`).
- SP-1, SP-2, SP-3 records in `docs/analysis/spikes/`; DO-6 WF-32, WF-33, WF-34 (`test_experiment_import`); M-29 definition.
- PRD R-48, PD-29; coverage audit OBS-5, OBS-6.
- **Brief check:** serves the brief's expectation of evidence for the choices made (spike results recorded as data); touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given the SP-2 fixture (20 runs per assertion, store p95), the importer writes one `experiment_run` holding the assertion results and store p95, and no `model_call` rows (WF-33) — verify: `import-spike.test.ts::test_experiment_import` (SP-2 fixture) — evidence: row; call count 0 — covers: R-33, OBS-6, M-19, M-24, M-27, M-36, M-37
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Given the SP-3 fixture (12 plants, caught and false flags per lesson), the importer writes one `experiment_run` with plant results (WF-34) — verify: `import-spike.test.ts::test_experiment_import` (SP-3 fixture) — evidence: row with caught counts — covers: GR-1, OBS-6, M-7, M-32, M-33
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] Importing the same report twice leaves `experiment_run` and `model_call` counts unchanged and the second `ImportReport.model_calls_imported` is 0 — verify: `import-spike.test.ts::idempotent_reimport` — evidence: counts before/after — covers: OBS-6
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] After importing SP-1, the build-spend query behind M-29 includes the imported calls (sum over `model_call.cost_usd` equals the SP-1 ledger total in the fixture) — verify: `import-spike.test.ts::build_spend_includes_spike_calls` — evidence: sum equality — covers: M-29, R-55

## [NL-88] prompts: save a guidance version and try it on one lesson

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-10 — As an author I change the guidance part of the prompt and try it on one lesson first, while the locked rules stay out of reach, so that I can improve drafts without breaking the rules that keep them safe. (Cut #7: if cut, the list and the locked layer remain, NL-34.)

### What to build
Add the write half of CON-24 to the `PromptService` NL-34 created (same file, **save path only**; the list path and wiring are NL-34's) and prove the trial path end to end.

- `PromptService.save_guidance(user, req: SaveGuidanceRequest) -> GuidanceVersion` (`saveGuidance`): role `author`; in one `TxRunner.with_tx`: validate `reason` non-empty (`REASON_REQUIRED` 422) and `guidance_text` ≤ 8,000 characters (`INVALID_REQUEST` 400 naming the field); `PromptRepo.insert_guidance(NewGuidanceVersion{base_version_id, guidance_text, reason, author_id}, diff)` where the repo row-locks and raises `STALE_BASE` 409 with `details.latest_version_id` unless `base_version_id` is the latest guidance version; compute the text `diff` against the base; `AuditLog.append`. The new version is immutable; running runs keep their pin (`pinned_by_runs`).
- `POST` handler added to `apps/web/app/api/prompt-versions/route.ts` through `with_route`.
- **Try on one lesson** is not a new endpoint: it is `startRun` with `kind "trial"` (NL-27) naming the new `prompt_version_id`, which creates one candidate job (CON-5 / CON-16): the candidate is a new version and never overwrites the current lesson. This ticket owns the test that proves the chain.

**Must not:** write the locked layer from any route (R-38, GR-18); edit a saved version; let a save change an already running run's pinned version; add a route other than POST on `prompt-versions`.

### Sources
- DO-4 §5 `PromptService.save_guidance`, `SaveGuidanceRequest`, §3.5 `PromptRepo.insert_guidance`, `NewGuidanceVersion`, `PromptVersionRow`, §10.1 (`STALE_BASE`, `REASON_REQUIRED`); DO-3 §2.3 (A16), §6 (`prompt_version`).
- CON-24 (agreed), CON-5 (trial run), CON-16 (candidate, never overwrite); OpenAPI `saveGuidance`.
- PRD R-38, R-39, GR-18, GR-10; UXQ-3 (guidance program-wide, pinned per run); WP-1 row 8 as the trial lesson; DO-6 WF-20.
- **Brief check:** serves the editable guidance layer with versions and a one-lesson trial while the locked layer stays unreachable; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given the current guidance v1, when an author posts `saveGuidance` with `base_version_id v1`, valid text and a reason, then 200 with version number 2, a stored `diff` against v1, the reason and the author, and v1 is unchanged (WF-20) — verify: `apps/web/app/api/prompt-versions/route.test.ts::save_creates_v2_with_diff_and_reason` — evidence: response; both rows — covers: R-39, CON-24, M-5
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] Given a run pinned to v1 and running, when v2 is saved, then the run's `prompt_version_id` is still v1 and `pinned_by_runs` of v1 lists it (WF-20) — verify: `route.test.ts::test_prompt_version_capture` — evidence: run row; list response — covers: R-38, CON-24
- [ ] AC-3 [failure/refusal] When the reason is empty then 422 `REASON_REQUIRED`; when `guidance_text` has 8,001 characters then 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `guidance_text`; neither writes a row — verify: `route.test.ts::reason_required_and_length_limit` — evidence: two responses; unchanged counts — covers: CON-24, CON-G2
- [ ] AC-4 [failure/refusal] Given two authors saving from base v1, then the first gets v2 and the second 409 `STALE_BASE` with `details.latest_version_id = v2`; no row is lost and the second write left no row (WF-20) — verify: `route.test.ts::concurrent_saves_stale_base` — evidence: two responses; version count — covers: CON-24, CON-G2
- [ ] AC-5 [failure/refusal] When a reviewer or approver posts a save then 403 `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` and no row or audit event is written — verify: `route.test.ts::role_forbidden_writes_nothing` — evidence: response; counts — covers: CON-24, CON-G1, R-54

## [NL-89] judge: OpenRouter adapter, judge job, verdict repository

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Platform ticket (cut #2, no user story of its own): a binary, advisory, provisional judge on a second provider (PD-12) reads one activity and one official standard and answers "does it teach this?". It adds a second provider key and sends lesson text off-box, so it is security work.

### What to build
Build the judge machinery; the trigger after store, the `judge_no` advisory issue and the claim loop are NL-110, and the calibration script is NL-111.

- `packages/llm/src/openrouter-judge.ts` — `OpenRouterJudgeAdapter implements JudgeClient` (DO-4 §2): the **only** module that calls OpenRouter. Constructor record `OpenRouterJudgeAdapter_ctor{api_key: SecretStr (OPENROUTER_API_KEY), model_id (MODEL_JUDGE_ID), timeout_ms}`. `verdict(JudgeRequest) -> JudgeVerdictResult{verdict "yes"|"no", rationale, served_model, usage, raw_text, provider_request_id}`: sends **only** `activity_text`, `standard_text`, the rubric and the question (no lesson id, user, email or other lesson text), parses a strict JSON verdict with Zod, raises `ProviderError` kinds on timeout / 429 / 5xx / unparsable output, never retries itself.
- `packages/llm/src/stub-judge.ts` — `StubJudgeClient implements JudgeClient` with scripted verdicts for tests and the stub mode (DO-4 names `stub.ts`; a separate file avoids editing NL-14's).
- `packages/db/src/repos/judge.ts` — `PgJudgeRepo.insert_verdict(NewJudgeVerdict) -> JudgeVerdictRow` into `judge_verdict` (`lesson_id`, `content_hash`, `address`, `code`, `question`, `verdict`, `model_call_id`, `served_model`); append-only.
- `apps/worker/src/judge/judge-job.ts` — `JudgeJob.run(lesson_id, content_hash) -> JudgeRunReport{pairs, verdicts_no, cost_usd}`: per (activity, standard) pair: `PromptRenderer.render_judge` → `SpendLedger.reserve` (`max_call_cost`; refusal skips the pair and counts it) → `ModelCallLog.insert_sent` **before** the call → `JudgeClient.verdict` → `ModelCallLog.complete` → `settle` (or `release` on failure) → `JudgeRepo.insert_verdict`. Every call is a `model_call` row (`purpose "judge"`, alias `JUDGE`). It writes **no** issue and never touches Approve (NL-110 adds the advisory issue).

**Must not:** send anything but the four inputs to OpenRouter; log or store the key; make a verdict block anything; skip the reservation; edit the generation path or `IssueRepo`.

### Sources
- DO-4 §2 `JudgeRequest`, `JudgeVerdictResult`, `JudgeClient`, `OpenRouterJudgeAdapter`, `StubJudgeClient`; §3.4 `ModelCallLog`, `SpendLedger`; §3.5 `NewJudgeVerdict`, `JudgeVerdictRow`, `JudgeRepo`; §4 `PromptRenderer.render_judge`, `JudgePromptInput`; §6 `JudgeJob`, `JudgeRunReport`; §12 `OpenRouterJudgeAdapter_ctor`; DO-3 §2.1, §2.4, §6 (`judge_verdict`).
- CON-13 (the `judge_no` issue kind is advisory; judge verdicts are provisional, R-23); DO-5 S12 (calibration gates use).
- PRD R-23, PD-12 (different provider), PD-28; GR-4, GR-10; WP-1; DO-6 WF-23.
- **Brief check:** serves the optional binary advisory judge on a different provider (R-23, cut #2); touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing (never blocks Approve) → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] Given the adapter pointed at a recorded HTTP fixture (no network), when `verdict` is called for one pair, then it returns `yes` or `no` with rationale, `served_model`, usage and `provider_request_id`, and the request body contains exactly `activity_text`, `standard_text`, the rubric and the question (WF-23) — verify: `packages/llm/src/openrouter-judge.test.ts::request_has_only_the_four_inputs` — evidence: request body key list — covers: R-23, GR-4
- [ ] AC-2 [negative] With distinctive markers in the lesson id, the author name and a second lesson's text, none appears in the outbound request body, headers or any log line; the `Authorization` header value appears only in the request itself, never in logs, `model_call` rows or errors (WF-23) — verify: `openrouter-judge.test.ts::no_identifiers_or_key_leak` — evidence: scan zero matches — covers: OBS-7, GR-9, GR-13
- [ ] AC-3 [failure/refusal] Given a timeout, a 429, a 5xx and an unparsable body, then each raises the matching `ProviderError` kind, the adapter does not retry, and `JudgeJob` records the pair as failed (a `model_call` of status `failed`) and releases its reservation (WF-23) — verify: `openrouter-judge.test.ts::provider_errors_map_to_kinds` and `apps/worker/src/judge/judge-job.test.ts::failed_call_releases_reservation` — evidence: error kinds; reservation released — covers: R-48, OBS-5
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] Given a lesson with 3 (activity, standard) pairs and `StubJudgeClient` scripted `yes, no, yes`, when `JudgeJob.run` runs, then 3 `model_call` rows (`purpose "judge"`, rendered prompt present before the call), 3 `judge_verdict` rows with the served model, `JudgeRunReport{pairs 3, verdicts_no 1}` and no `issue` row is written (WF-23) — verify: `judge-job.test.ts::test_judge_capture` — evidence: rows and report — covers: R-23, OBS-5, M-6
- [ ] AC-5 [invariant] The judge never blocks: after `run`, Approve's gate state for the lesson has no judge-derived blocking or confirmation issue (the gate reads only `issue` rows, none written here) (WF-23) — verify: `judge-job.test.ts::verdicts_never_enter_the_gate` — evidence: `approve_gate` result unchanged — covers: R-23, GR-4
- [ ] AC-6 [failure/refusal] Given `FakeSpendLedger` refusing (`run_cap`) for the second pair, then no `model_call` row exists for that pair, the report counts it skipped, and the job continues with the others (WF-23) — verify: `judge-job.test.ts::spend_refusal_skips_pair_without_call` — evidence: call rows; report — covers: R-55, M-29
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] `PgJudgeRepo.insert_verdict` is append-only: an UPDATE or DELETE on `judge_verdict` raises (DDL trigger, NL-08), and two verdicts for the same pair on different hashes coexist — verify: `packages/db/src/repos/judge.int.test.ts::append_only_and_per_hash` — evidence: trigger error; rows — covers: R-35, R-23
- [ ] AC-8 [invariant] With `MODEL_PROVIDER_MODE=stub` the composition builds `StubJudgeClient`; the adapter is constructed only when mode is `real` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is present, else construction fails naming the variable (never its value) — verify: `apps/worker/src/judge/judge-job.test.ts::adapter_only_in_real_mode_with_key` — evidence: build outcomes — covers: OBS-7, PD-12
- [ ] AC-9 [capture] Given the real worker entry for the judge job on the stub, when `test_judge_capture` runs, then one `judge_verdict` row per pair carries the served model, each pair has its `model_call_id`, and none blocks Approve (WF-23) — verify: `apps/worker/src/judge/judge-job.test.ts::test_judge_capture` — evidence: rows — covers: OBS-1, OBS-5, M-6, M-34
- [ ] AC-10 [regression/context] area map row(s) for `packages/llm/src/openrouter-judge.ts`, `packages/llm/src/stub-judge.ts`, `apps/worker/src/judge/**`, `packages/db/src/repos/judge.ts` planned → actual (A19 judge (DO-3 §2.4, §4)); router/ICM rows if a route's evidence changed; dev-log entry (Changed · Why · Checked · Remaining); the slice plan's wiring-owner row ticked where this ticket fills one — verify: `git diff --stat` and `python3 ~/.claude/skills/icm-project/scripts/check_context.py .` — evidence: diff touches only those rows; no FAIL — covers: OBS-11

Acceptance anchor: WP-1 (`docs/data/worked-pairs.md`): Lesson 4's activities and standards give the three pairs in AC-4. Frozen-test note (`risk::security`, `.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`): `test-writer-agent` freezes failing tests for AC-1…AC-9 from these criteria before the implementer starts (manifest and tamper check apply); the security agent reads this ticket's diff at the wave merge.

### What to build
Write the coverage read.

- `apps/web/src/server/services/coverage-service.ts` — `CoverageService.coverage(user, unit_id) -> CoverageMatrix` (CON-22, DO-4 §5): **one query** over stored alignment links (`AlignmentRepo.coverage_rows(unit_id)`) joined to `standard` for the official text, never a model. Response `standards` (`code`, `official_text`, `never_assessed`), `lessons` (`lesson_id`, `number`) and `cells` (`code`, `lesson_id`, `roles` any of I / P / A, `confirmed_by` `person | judge_only | generator_only`, `source` `approved | working`). A lesson's cells read its latest approved snapshot where one exists (`source approved`), else its stored derived row (`working`). A code is `never_assessed` when no cell has role `A`.
- `apps/web/app/api/units/[unitId]/coverage/route.ts` (GET) through `with_route`; every role reads; unknown unit → `NOT_FOUND`.
- `apps/web/src/server/wiring/coverage.ts` — `wire_coverage` returns `CoverageWiring{coverage: CoverageService}`. It lives in its **own file**; it does not edit `BoardService` or `wiring/metrics.ts` (DO-4 §5, A18: this resolves the slice plan's `board-service.ts` coverage-method row in favour of DO-4; the dependency on NL-54 stays harmlessly).

Per-cell `source` (`approved` / `working`, CON-22) comes from `CoverageCell.source`, chosen inside `AlignmentRepo.coverage_rows` in its one query (NL-43; DO-4 §3.5, §13 R-11); the service groups cells by `(code, lesson_id)` into `roles` and passes `confirmed_by` and `source` through unchanged.

**Must not:** call a model; write anything; return minutes or reviewer names; edit repositories you do not own.

- CON-22 (agreed); OpenAPI `getCoverageMatrix`.
