## [NL-115] integration: CON-18 submit, approve by a second account on the pinned version, send back, reopen

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-24…US-28 and US-31 — As a reviewer I submit a lesson when nothing blocks it; as an approver, a second person, I approve one pinned version on its evidence and rate how usable the draft was; I can send a lesson back with a reason, approve linked lessons in order, and reopen an approved lesson without breaking its dependants. This is the product's central promise (R-33, HP-5), proved on the real stack.

### What to build
Drive WF-15 end to end with Playwright and API tests on the Compose stack (stub provider, two browser contexts for two accounts) and fix the seams on SCR-14, SCR-15 and SCR-9's submit action.

- Owns: `apps/web/e2e/integration/con-18/**`, `apps/web/src/features/workspace/actions/submit/**`, SCR-14 (Approval review) and SCR-15 (Send back or reopen) and their TRACEABILITY rows (SCR-9 row: append only).
- Flows: `start_review` and `submit` (web checks role and state → collaboration internal freeze: lock, store at once, state-vector cover check, blocking checks on the stored row, snapshot + state + transition in one transaction, `read_only` mode); `withdraw`; `approve` by a different account pinned to the snapshot hash and state vector with a rating (re-checks the snapshot, writes approval snapshot, audit row, and at the first approval the frozen metrics row once); `request_changes`; `reopen` (new version from the approved snapshot).
- Error precedence per CON-18: `ROLE_FORBIDDEN` → `NOT_FOUND` → `INVALID_TRANSITION` → `NOTE_REQUIRED` / `REASON_REQUIRED` / `RATING_REQUIRED` → `NOT_STORED` → `STALE_PIN` → `FOUR_EYES` → `SUGGESTION_PENDING` → `BLOCKED` → `CONFIRMATION_OPEN` → `DEPENDENCY_UNAPPROVED`.
- **risk::security:** a bug here approves content nobody reviewed or lets one person approve their own work. `test-writer-agent` freezes AC-3 to AC-8 and AC-11 as failing tests before the implementer starts (frozen-test manifest and tamper check apply); `security-privacy-agent` reads this diff at the wave merge.
- Must not: add any route taking more than one lesson, edit `decide_transition` (NL-21), the freeze command (NL-106) or the metrics writer (NL-48) — defects found there go back to their tickets.

### Sources
- CON-18 (agreed: actions, roles, named errors, precedence, guarantees; UXP-1, UXP-2, UXP-4, UXP-6, UXP-10, GAP-2); SCR-9, SCR-14, SCR-15 (signed); DO-6 WF-15; DO-5 S5, S13
- DO-4 §5 `TransitionService`, §3.3 `CollabCommands.lock_and_snapshot`; SP-2 record (`docs/analysis/spikes/SP-2*.md`); HP-5, HP-8, HP-10
- PRD R-33, R-34, R-35, R-49, R-60, GR-6, GR-15; WP-1, WP-4
- **Brief check:** serves "Have a UI/UX for approval workflow for lessons within a unit, where once reviewed/updated it is flagged as complete in our system."; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

Fill the web assist wiring and prove WF-14 end to end on the real stack with the stub model.

- Owns: `apps/web/src/server/wiring/assist.ts` (builds `SuggestionService` with the real `PaidCaller`, `PromptRenderer.render_assist`, `SuggestionRepo`, `CollabCommands`), `apps/web/e2e/integration/con-17/**`, SCR-13 (AI assist panel) and its TRACEABILITY row.
- Flow: `requestSuggestion` (anchor, ≤ 2,000-char `selected_text`, note) → synchronous stub call (20 s timeout) → `pending` suggestion held outside the document; `listSuggestions` after reload; `decideSuggestion` accept → collaboration server resolves the anchor against the live document, compares its text with the stored `selected_text`, replaces it in one transaction tagged `ai-assist` attributed to the acceptor, stores; reject → discarded and logged; a pending suggestion closes itself after 30 min.
- **risk::security:** untrusted model text enters a document. `test-writer-agent` freezes AC-3, AC-4, AC-6, AC-7 and AC-8 first; `security-privacy-agent` reads the diff at the wave merge.
- Must not: apply an accept from the client, trust `anchored_text_now`, offer assist on an approved lesson, or send anything but the selected text, note and the lesson's own context to the model.

### Sources
- CON-17 (agreed: `requestSuggestion`, `listSuggestions`, `decideSuggestion`, named errors, guarantees); SCR-13 (signed); DO-6 WF-14; DO-4 §5 `SuggestionService`, §3.3 apply-edit
- PRD R-31, GR-7, GR-1, GR-2, R-58; HP-5; WP-1
- **Brief check:** serves "AI assisted tooling as helpful"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

## [NL-118] capacity: HTTP load probe for the 200-user mix (R-57 as amended, PD-33)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — As Innocent I need honest page-speed numbers at the 200-user spike (PD-33: 500 users a day, 200 at once). This ticket builds the HTTP load script and proves it measures correctly with a small run; NL-127 runs the real 200-user spike on the VPS.

### What to build
Build the HTTP half of the S14 capacity probe (A20; DO-4 §9 `SpikeOptions`, `run_spike`; DO-3 §4 `load/spike.ts`).

- Files: `load/spike.ts` (fills NL-49's shell), `load/http-mix.ts` (virtual-user behaviours and the schedule), `load/stats.ts` (percentiles, windows, recovery), tests. Command: `npm run load:spike -- --users 200 --ramp-s 120 --plateau-s 900` (NL-127 runs it; here a small run proves it).
- **The mix** (`docs/design/capacity-and-workload.md` *Workload assumptions*), as shares of `users`: 70% reviewers open a lesson (CON-11) then send a heartbeat (CON-20) every 15 s; 20% poll the unit board (CON-9) or run progress (CON-6) every 2 s; 10% authors and approvers act about once per 10 s (a mix of reads and one safe write class); everyone loads a page about once per 30 s. Burst shape: 2-minute ramp, 15-minute plateau, 2-minute ramp down.
- **Safety of the data:** virtual users sign in as seeded synthetic-flagged accounts (`synthetic` is seed-only, CON-1); their heartbeats are stored but excluded from minutes (CON-20); the script never writes lesson content or a transition, so demo data and the north-star numbers stay clean. If the seed script (NL-82) has no synthetic probe accounts, that is a gap raised to the batch merge agent, not an edit to `ops/seed.ts`.
- Provider stubbed: `provider_mode` is `stub` only and the script refuses `real`.
- Output: one `ProbeRunRecord` (`kind: "http"`, `users`, `duration_s`, `machine`, `provider_mode`, `p95_ms` for `lesson_open`, `board`, `poll`, `error_rate` (5xx + socket drops ÷ requests + sessions), `max_db_connections` sampled each second from `pg_stat_activity`, `event_loop_lag_p95_ms` = the load script's own lag, `n`) through `EvidenceRepo.insert_probe_run`. Server-side event-loop lag is not measured by this ticket; the report says so. Recovery time (M-23) = time from plateau end until each p95 window is back within 10% of the pre-spike window.
- Must not: touch lesson content, run against a real provider, or edit any route.

### Sources
- `docs/design/capacity-and-workload.md` (mix, burst shape, targets, recovery criteria, *How capacity is validated*); DO-5 S14; DO-4 §9 and `ProbeRunRecord` (§3.4); DO-6 WF-29
- CON-9, CON-11, CON-20 (agreed; CON-20 heartbeat timing and author exclusion); PRD R-57 (as amended, §5.4), PD-33
- **Brief check:** serves "Rest of workflow and loading/editing of lessons should be performant and be able to handle staff of 20+ reviewers"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] WF-29: for 200 users the generated schedule over a 60 s plateau window is within ±10% of the capacity doc's mix: about 9.3 heartbeats/s, 20 polls/s, 2 requests/s, 6.7 page loads/s (computed without a server) — verify: `npx vitest run load/http-mix.test.ts -t schedule_matches_capacity_doc` — evidence: pass; the four rates printed with their ±10% bounds — covers: R-57, EV-S14, M-21
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] WF-29: percentiles, error rate and recovery time are computed correctly from fixed samples (known p95 of 1..100 ms; 3 of 300 requests failing gives 1.0%; windows returning within 10% at second 95 give 95 s) — verify: `npx vitest run load/stats.test.ts` — evidence: pass — covers: R-57, M-18, M-22, M-23
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] WF-29: a 5-user, 10-second probe against the Compose stack writes one `probe_run` row with p95s for `lesson_open`, `board`, `poll`, `n`, machine, `provider_mode = stub`, `max_db_connections` and the script's own loop lag — verify: `test_probe_writes_run` via `npx vitest run load/spike.int.test.ts` — evidence: pass; row read back by SQL — covers: R-57, EV-S14, EV-R1, OBS-6
- [ ] AC-4 [negative] WF-29: the probe leaves product data alone: after the run `lesson_doc`, `lesson_version`, `review_event` and `lesson_metrics` row counts and the north-star tile numbers are identical, and every heartbeat it sent belongs to a synthetic account — verify: same test, `-t leaves_data_alone` — evidence: counts equal; synthetic share 100% — covers: GR-15, CON-20, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-5 [failure/refusal] WF-29: `--provider real` is refused with exit 2 and no request is sent; a probe whose server returns `SERVICE_BUSY` records those as errors, not as slow successes — verify: `npm run load:spike -- --provider real; echo $?` and `-t busy_is_error` — evidence: exit 2; busy counted in `error_rate` — covers: R-55, CON-9
- [ ] AC-6 [invariant] WF-29: the report writer states git SHA, machine (cores and memory), stub-versus-real, `n`, targets (open < 1.5 s, poll < 300 ms, errors < 0.5%, recovery ≤ 2 min) and, for each missed target, the capacity doc's scale-path step — verify: `npx vitest run load/report.test.ts` writing `evals/reports/load-<date>.md` to a temp dir — evidence: pass; the five fields present; a forced miss lists a scale-path step — covers: EV-R1, EV-S14, M-20, M-23

## [NL-119] capacity: Yjs socket load script (R-56 as amended)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — As Innocent I need to know whether co-editing holds up at the spike: remote edit p95 < 500 ms, stored p95 < 3 s, zero lost acknowledged updates. Cuttable (#1): if cut, the docs say Yjs latency was not measured.

### What to build
Build the Yjs half of the S14 probe (A20; `load/yjs-mix.ts`, DO-4 §9 `SpikeOptions.socket_editors`, `ProbeRunRecord kind: "yjs"`).

- Files: `load/yjs-mix.ts`, `load/yjs-stats.ts`, tests; `load/spike.ts` (NL-118's) calls `run_yjs_mix` when `socket_editors > 0`; this ticket adds only that call site behind a flag and does not change HTTP behaviour.
- Editors: simulated Hocuspocus clients (session-authenticated like a browser, CON-12) spread over synthetic lessons of a dedicated load unit (never the demo unit), at most 3 per lesson; about 25% typing at one update per 2 s (the capacity doc's ~17.5 updates/s at 200 users). Each edit inserts a unique token `[<editor>-<seq>]` so loss is countable.
- Measures: remote-edit-visible p95 (sender's update to a co-editor's observed update), stored p95 (to the `stored` acknowledgement), **lost updates** (every acknowledged token must be present after a fresh reload at the end), socket error rate, reconnect time p95 after forced drops of about 5% of sockets (M-24).
- Must not: edit lessons of the demo unit, fix a collaboration defect (a defect is a finding, not a patch), or run with a real provider.

### Sources

- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] WF-30: lost-update counting is correct: a fixture where 2 of 100 acknowledged tokens are missing after reload reports `lost_updates = 2`, and a clean run reports 0 — verify: `npx vitest run load/yjs-stats.test.ts -t lost_updates` — evidence: pass — covers: R-56, M-19

## [NL-120] experiment: error-analysis round — ~20 traces, first failure each, `FT-N` taxonomy, models × failures; `gate::human` (Innocent ✓, PD-32 fallback)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — the build's numbers need their causes, not only their counts. Zero-to-hero §9 and GP-21/GP-51 say no tuning change lands without a named failure type; this ticket produces the named failure types (`FT-N`) from what the full run (NL-112) actually did, so NL-128…130 each change one thing against one `FT-N`.

### What to build
Read about 20 stored traces from the NL-112 run to their **first failure only**, file each under an `FT-N` written from what was seen, and write the table the experiments rest on. Output lives in `docs/testing/error-analysis/` (new; this ticket owns it).

**Method (DO-5 *Failure categories*; `docs/design/eval-plan.md`):**
1. **Pick the traces (about 20 of 47).** All lessons that ended `generation_failed`; all with a blocking issue after the repair; every lesson whose first draft needed the repair; then fill to about 20 with a seeded-random draw (seed written in the file) across lesson types. List the chosen `lesson_job` ids and why each was picked.
2. **Read each trace to its first failure.** From the stored rows (`model_call` rendered prompt and raw output, `issue`, `lesson_version`) via the operator's read-only SQL or the run summary (CON-21); never the restricted folder. Stop at the first thing that went wrong; do not catalogue later damage. Record: lesson id, step that first failed, one quoted line of evidence, the starting category (FC-1…FC-14) it falls under.
3. **Write `FT-N`s from what was seen.** Rename, split or merge FC-n as the traces demand; each `FT-N` has a one-sentence definition, the count, an example trace id, and where the fix would live (prompt layer, schema, check, compiler, code). Operational failures (429, timeout, cap) are not quality failures (GP-58): list them apart.
4. **Models × failures table.** Rows `FT-N`, columns the models and prompt versions the traces ran on (all `claude-sonnet-5-5` prompt v1 unless the run shows otherwise; the table says so rather than inventing columns).
5. **Recommend, do not run.** End with at most three candidate experiments, each: one `FT-N`, one variable, the expected effect, cost to score on the frozen set. These become NL-128/129/130; slots without a warranted `FT-N` are closed unused (slice plan open item 7).
6. **Human gate.** Innocent reviews the taxonomy and the candidate list (`gate::human`). Under PD-32 (his standing authorization) Claude's recommendation stands if he has not answered when the next dependent ticket is ready; the issue then records "adopted under PD-32 fallback, not reviewed by Innocent" and the dev log says the same. Unreviewed traces never become eval cases (DO-5 *Case provenance*): promotion to `promoted-trace` happens only after his review.

Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

### Sources
- DO-5 `docs/design/eval-plan.md` *Failure categories* (FC-1…FC-14, the `FT-N` rule), *Case provenance*; `docs/design/hard-problems.md` (HP-1…HP-10 "How we'll know it worked")
- NL-112's report and run traces; NL-108's kickoff page (flow, prompts with versions, failure types)
- Rules: `.claude/rules/` verification-evals-observability (error analysis first, one variable, frozen set); GP-21, GP-51, GP-58 in `docs/principles/`
- PRD PD-32 (standing authorization), PD-28 (rewritten lessons become traces)
- **Brief check:** serves "Thoughtful design and easy to understand/use/navigate workflow" by tying every later change to an observed failure; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] about 20 traces were read to their first failure and each is filed under one `FT-N` (WF-25) — verify: `ls docs/testing/error-analysis/` and `grep -cE '^\| *lesson_job' docs/testing/error-analysis/*.md` — evidence: a trace table of 18–22 rows, each with lesson id, first failing step, one quoted evidence line, starting FC-n and final `FT-N`; the selection rule and random seed are written down — covers: R-51, EV-S9
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] the taxonomy and the models × failures table are written from the traces, with counts that add up (WF-25) — verify: `python3 -c` count of table rows per `FT-N` against the per-trace table — evidence: each `FT-N` has a definition, count, example id and fix location; row counts sum to the traces read; operational failures are listed separately and not counted as wrong answers — covers: M-5, M-31
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] at most three candidate experiments are named, each tied to one `FT-N` and one variable — verify: read of the *Candidate experiments* section — evidence: each candidate states the `FT-N`, the single variable, expected effect and cost; a slot with no warranted `FT-N` is marked closed unused — covers: R-51
- [ ] AC-4 [negative] nothing from the restricted folder and no unreviewed trace promoted to an eval case — verify: `git grep -nE 'restricted/originals' docs/testing/` and `git diff --name-only -- evals/cases` — evidence: no match; no case file changed — covers: GR-9, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-5 [human] Innocent's review (or the PD-32 fallback) is recorded on the issue — verify: his reply quoted, or the line "adopted under PD-32 fallback, not reviewed by Innocent" — evidence: whichever applies, labelled human-only or fallback, plus the dev-log line — covers: —

### Observability

## [NL-121] evals: held-out structural comparison, counts only, written outside tracked files

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — As Innocent I want to know how close the generated unit's structure is to Newsela's published Unit 4, without that published content ever entering a prompt, a report or the repo. A local script compares counts only (R-53, PD-20). Cuttable (#2).

### What to build
Build the local held-out comparison (A20; DO-5 S11; DO-6 WF-27).

- Files: `evals/src/heldout/**` (`cli.ts`, `compare.ts`, `schema.ts`, tests), `evals/src/suites/s11.ts`; output `evals/local/held-out/<date>.json`, which is git-ignored (add nothing to `.gitignore` here: A0 owns it. The check below proves the path is already ignored; if not, raise it to the batch merge agent). Command: `npm run eval:heldout`.
- **Handling rule (source register, PD-20):** only this script, on this machine, reads `docs/source/restricted/originals/lessons-json/`. It compares counts: per generated lesson, lesson-type match, section-sequence match, focus-standard overlap, against the published lesson at the same number. Its report is `z.strictObject` of integers and rates only: no string field except fixed keys, no title, no text, no id from the published files.
- The script imports no model client and no HTTP library (enforced by the boundaries lint). A parse failure prints the lesson **number** only, never content.
- **No agent opens the restricted folder or its files.** Tests use a synthetic stand-in at `evals/tests/fixtures/heldout-syn/` with a canary string; the real run is the script's own process reading the folder, and the agent reads back only the numbers file.
- **risk::security** (held-out data kept out of tracked files): `test-writer-agent` freezes AC-1 to AC-6 first; `security-privacy-agent` reads this diff at the wave merge.
- Must not: write the report to a tracked path, put published text in a log, an error, a database row or an issue comment, or quote more than the headline counts in docs.

### Sources
- DO-5 S11 (*Development and held-out separation*, handling rule); source register *Handling rule for restricted material*; PD-20; DO-6 WF-27
- PRD R-53, GR-9, GR-11; DO-7 M-42; `.claude/rules/synthetic-test-data.md`
- **Brief check:** serves "Please use the example(s) from the lesson format/structure link above to identify the sections and structure of the lessons"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

## [NL-122] judge: Innocent labels ~30 (activity, standard) pairs

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Delivery (R-23, cut #2) — the advisory judge may only be shown once it agrees with a person. Innocent's labels are the expected answer (DO-5 *Expected-answer authority*: a model is never its own authority). Why now: the labels need real activities from the full run, and the judge calibration (NL-132) cannot run without them.

### What to build
**What Innocent does (only he can label; `gate::human`).** About 45–60 minutes.
1. Claude prepares `evals/judge/labels.csv` (a tracked file, no lesson text beyond the one activity per row) with about 30 rows chosen from the NL-112 lessons: columns `pair_id, lesson_ref, activity_text, standard_code, standard_text, label, note`. `label` is empty. Claude draws the pairs so about 40% are clear yeses, about 40% clear noes and the rest borderline, and says so on the issue **without marking which row is which**. The split into 20 for calibration and 10 held back is fixed by Claude by a seeded draw and written in `evals/judge/split.json` (git-tracked, committed before labelling). Innocent does not need to see the split.
2. For each row he answers one question: **"Does this activity teach or check this standard?"** `1` = yes, `0` = no. A `note` is optional (one line on why, useful for the rubric). He fills the `label` column in the VS Code editor on `claude-vultr`, or tells Claude the labels in the chat and Claude enters them verbatim.
3. He says "labels done" on the issue. If he prefers not to build the judge, he says "no judge" instead: cut #2 then fires, Claude closes NL-110, NL-111, NL-132 and this ticket as unused, and the docs say "Alignment is checked by code and confirmed by a named reviewer; no model judge in this build" (PRD §6.4).

**What Claude records afterwards.** Counts only: rows labelled, yes/no split, the date; the 20/10 split file hash; one dev-log line; `.claude/state/resume.md` next action (NL-132). Claude never edits a label to match the judge, never shows the judge the 10 held-back labels while tuning (DO-5 *Development and held-out separation*), and never labels a pair itself.

### Sources
- DO-5 `docs/design/eval-plan.md` S12 (*Scoring*, *Acceptance conditions*, *Development and held-out separation*); DO-6 WF-31; DO-7 M-34
- PRD R-23, PD-12 (judge on another provider), PD-17 / §6.4 (cut #2); CON-13 (the judge's `judge_no` issues)
- NL-110 (advisory judge), NL-111 (calibration script reads this file)
- **Brief check:** serves "AI-assisted tools" for review only as an advisory aid and refuses to show any judge verdict before it agrees with a person; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [human] about 30 rows are labelled by Innocent, binary, none by Claude (WF-31) — verify: `awk -F, 'NR>1 && $6!="" {n++} END {print n}' evals/judge/labels.csv` and Innocent's "labels done" reply — evidence: 28–32 labelled rows, every `label` is `0` or `1`; the reply quoted and labelled human-only evidence — covers: R-23, EV-S12
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] the 20/10 split was committed before labelling and the held-back 10 are not used for tuning (WF-31) — verify: `git log --format=%h\ %s -- evals/judge/split.json evals/judge/labels.csv` — evidence: `split.json` commit precedes the first commit that adds a label; split has 20 calibration and 10 held-back `pair_id`s with no overlap — covers: EV-S12, M-34
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] the file holds only the activity text and standard text needed to label, nothing from the restricted folder (WF-31) — verify: `git grep -nE 'restricted/originals' evals/judge/` and read of three random rows — evidence: no match; each `activity_text` appears in the NL-112 stored lesson it names — covers: GR-9, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-4 [failure] "no judge" is a valid answer: if Innocent says it, cut #2 is recorded, not argued (WF-31) — verify: his reply quoted and the dev-log line — evidence: NL-110/111/132 closed as unused with the PRD §6.4 sentence in `SUBMISSION.md` notes; or this AC marked n/a because labels were given — covers: R-23
- [ ] AC-5 [regression/context] dev-log entry and `.claude/state/resume.md` next action — verify: `git diff --name-only` — evidence: only `evals/judge/labels.csv`, `evals/judge/split.json`, the dev-log file and `.claude/state/resume.md`

Acceptance anchor: none — a human labelling task; its output is the expected-answer set for S12.

### Observability
- Responsibilities: WF-31 (judge calibration) reads this file when NL-132 runs; this ticket writes no record itself. Labels live in a tracked CSV, never in the database.
- Capture evidence: N/A for this human ticket; the calibration capture check is NL-111's (`test_calibration_record`) and NL-132 AC-4

### Evaluation

- Expected-answer authority: Innocent's labels (DO-5 *Expected-answer authority*, row "Activity teaches / checks a standard")

## [NL-123] ops: Innocent's measured review sessions (reviewer + approver accounts), two stopwatch reviews, approver ratings on the demo lessons

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-30 — As a content lead (P-3), I need the board's north-star tile to show the median active minutes per approved lesson with its *n* …, so that the number can't be read as a saving it isn't. US-25 and US-31 add the approve-on-the-pinned-version step and the one-click rating. Only Innocent's own reviews are human sessions (PD-25, amended); every Claude-driven session is `synthetic` and excluded. These sessions give the north-star tile its first honest numbers and S8's stopwatch check its reference.

### What to build
**What Innocent does (only he can review as a human; `gate::human`).** About 60–75 minutes in all, in the real app on the release-candidate stack.
1. **Setup (Claude, before).** Stack up from the committed Compose config with the NL-112 unit loaded; two demo accounts exist, **reviewer** and **approver** (NL-82; one person, two roles, labelled as such, PD-25). Claude gives Innocent the URL, both logins (from the seeded-account note, never in this issue), and the three lesson addresses: the WP-1 lesson (row 8, L4), the WP-2 lesson (row 9), the WP-3 lesson (row 25).
2. **Two stopwatch reviews (reviewer account).** For the WP-1 lesson and the WP-3 lesson: sign in as the reviewer, start a phone stopwatch the moment you open the lesson (that is `start_review`), review it as you would for real (read, fix what you would fix, resolve any confirmation), pause the stopwatch if you leave the screen, stop it at **Submit**. Keep one browser tab, in focus; do not leave the lesson open and idle. Tell Claude: lesson, stopwatch minutes, any pauses.
3. **Approve and rate three lessons (approver account).** Sign in as the approver (the account that did **not** last edit the lesson), open each of the three lessons from the review queue, read the evidence checklist, **Approve** on the pinned version and choose the rating: *usable as drafted* / *usable with edits* / *rewritten*. Rate honestly; a *rewritten* is a useful result (it becomes an error-analysis trace, PD-28). The WP-2 lesson needs a reviewer pass first (use the reviewer account for a normal short review, no stopwatch).
4. Say "sessions done" on the issue.

**What Claude records afterwards (never drives these sessions).** From stored rows only: per lesson, computed active minutes (`lesson_metrics.active_minutes`) beside the stopwatch minutes and the percentage difference; the three ratings; the board tile as shown (median, *n*, G-2, "approved k of N", caption). Claude does not edit a session, a heartbeat or a rating, and labels every number "one reviewer, n = k" (PD-25, GR-15). The synthetic NL-99 scripted-review rows stay in the database and stay excluded.

### Sources

### Acceptance criteria

## [NL-124] seeded errors: ~5 planted by Claude, reviewed by Innocent through the normal flow

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-34 — As a content lead (P-3), I need … the seeded-error catch rate, each with its *n*, so that I can judge the drafts and the review, not just the speed. M-4 (G-3) is the guard on the north star: reviewer minutes only mean something if review still catches planted errors. The test is only fair if the reviewer does not know where the errors are (R-52).

### What to build
**What Claude does first (the planter; `npm run eval:seed`, NL-92).** Plan about 5 errors on copies of lessons from the NL-112 unit, of different kinds, including the **"wrong code" plant** (a focus-standard code outside the row's lists, which must be caught: the S10 floor) and, for example, an invented quote, a page number out of range, a missing teaching link, minutes outside 50 ± 5. No model call is needed: `npm run eval:seed -- --plan <hidden key>`. The key (which lesson, which error) is written to the git-ignored `evals/local/seed-key.json` and **is never shown to Innocent or placed in the issue** until the run ends.

**What Innocent does (blind review; `gate::human`).** About 45–60 minutes. Claude gives him one sentence: "Review these lessons as you normally would and approve what you would approve; do not look for anything in particular." Then:
1. Sign in as the **reviewer** account; open each lesson in the seeded set from the review queue (SCR-9), read, fix what you would fix, resolve what the checks raise, and **Submit** or **Request changes** exactly as you would for real.
2. Sign in as the **approver** account (not the last editor): open each submitted lesson (SCR-14) and **Approve** or **Send back**. Do not skip a lesson because it "looks planted"; the number only means something if you treat each as real.
3. Say "seeded review done" on the issue. Do not open `evals/local/` and do not ask how many there were.

**What Claude records afterwards.** Only after "done": unseal the key, match each planted error to what happened (caught by a check, caught by the reviewer, caught at approval, or **missed and approved**), and hand the scoring to NL-135. Claude plants the errors and never reviews or approves them (the planter is not the reviewer); the synthetic accounts are not used for the review.

### Sources
- DO-5 S10 (`docs/design/eval-plan.md`: *Scoring*, *Acceptance conditions*, *Development and held-out separation* — "the R-52 answer key"); DO-6 WF-26; DO-7 M-4
- NL-92 (planting tool and report); CON-18; SCR-9, SCR-14 (signed)
- PRD R-52 (§5.4), G-3, §6.4 cut #6, PD-1
- **Brief check:** serves "a solution for improving productivity of internal staff" by checking that faster review does not mean missed errors; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] about 5 errors are planted by Claude, of different kinds, including the wrong-code plant, with the key sealed (WF-26) — verify: `npm run eval:seed -- --plan <key> --dry-run` output and `ls -l evals/local/seed-key.json`, `git check-ignore evals/local/seed-key.json` — evidence: 4–6 planted errors listed by kind only; the key file exists and is git-ignored; the issue shows kinds, not locations — covers: R-52, EV-S10
- [ ] AC-2 [human] Innocent reviews and approves or sends back each seeded lesson through the normal flow, not told which are planted (WF-26) — verify: his "seeded review done" reply and the `review_event` rows for the seeded lessons — evidence: every seeded lesson has a reviewer move and an approver move recorded by the human accounts; reply quoted and labelled human-only evidence — covers: R-52, M-4
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] the planter was not the reviewer, and the key stayed hidden until the run ended (WF-26) — verify: `git log --format=%h\ %an\ %s -- evals/local` (should be empty, ignored) and the timestamps of the issue comment unsealing the key against "seeded review done" — evidence: the unseal comes after "done"; no `audit_event` by the synthetic accounts on the seeded lessons — covers: EV-S10, CON-G4
- [ ] AC-4 [capture] each planted error has a recorded result row (WF-26) — verify: `psql` on `eval_run` and `eval_case_result` for the seeded run, plus `audit_event` for the review moves — evidence: one `eval_case_result` per planted error with outcome (caught by check / caught by reviewer / caught at approval / missed) and the hidden answer in `expected_json`; the planted-by and reviewed-by users differ — covers: OBS-6, OBS-1
- [ ] AC-5 [negative] the sealed key and the lessons' planted locations appear in no tracked file, log line or issue text before the run ends — verify: `git grep -n 'seed-key' -- ':!docs/plans'` and read of the issue thread — evidence: no tracked file contains key content — covers: R-52, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-6 [regression/context] dev-log entry and `.claude/state/resume.md` next action (NL-135 scoring) — verify: `git diff --name-only` — evidence: only the dev-log file and `.claude/state/resume.md` (the seeded data lives in the database, the key in an ignored file)

Acceptance anchor: none — a human blind review; its answer key is the planter's hidden file.

### Observability

- Capture evidence: AC-4

### Evaluation

- Scope boundary / refusal: planter never reviews; key sealed until "done"; cut #6 (if cut, the docs say seeded errors were not run)

## [NL-125] evals: S5 integrity e2e, 20 trials per assertion, 3 browser contexts

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-24, US-25 — Submit freezes the lesson and Approve pins the exact version reviewed. S5 repeats the promise 20 times per assertion with three live browsers, so a race that shows up once in twenty is caught before the demo (HP-4, HP-5).

### What to build
Build the S5 integrity suite (A20; DO-5 S5; DO-6 WF-43).

- Files: `apps/web/e2e/integrity/**` (Playwright specs and a trial driver, 3 browser contexts), `evals/src/suites/s5.ts` (records results), report `evals/reports/integrity-<git-sha>.md`. Command: `npm run test:e2e -- integrity --trials 20`.
- One trial = a fresh clone of a WP-1 stub lesson and three contexts: A (reviewer, editing), B (second reviewer, co-editing), C (approver). Assertions per trial (each stored as one `eval_case_result` with its trial number):
  1. **stale approve**: B edits after C loaded the snapshot (via withdraw / resubmit) → C's approve gets `STALE_PIN` 409 and nothing changes (WF-15);
  2. **zero edits after lock**: after Submit, A types → refused, the editor drops the refused local edits and tells the typist (CON-12 `refused`, `refused_from`), and no `lesson_doc`/`audit_event` row appears (WF-9);
  3. **zero silent keystroke loss**: every keystroke before Submit either appears in the stored snapshot or in the refused notice;
  4. **four-eyes**: the last stored editor cannot approve (WF-15);
  5. **pending suggestion blocks Approve**: run only if NL-116 landed, otherwise recorded `not built (cut #8)`, never as a pass;
  6. **round-trip hash identity**: JSON → Y.Doc → JSON hash unchanged after reload; and export hash = snapshot hash only if NL-102 landed (else `not built`).
- Store p95 across trials is recorded (target ≤ 500 ms `[A] → SP-2`). All floor-1.00 assertions need 20 of 20.
- Must not: edit editor, collaboration or transition code; a failing assertion is a bug report to its owner, not a patch here.

### Sources

## [NL-126] UX-5b: connected-app walkthrough, Lighthouse, `QA_REPORT.md`, every UX-5a row linked

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Delivery (no single US; all core stories) — UX-5a proved each screen against the mock as it was built; UX-5b proves the whole product against the connected application before Innocent signs it off (NL-133). Why: the brief judges "Thoughtful design and easy to understand/use/navigate workflow", and the demo shows the real stack, so a screen that works on the mock but not on the backend must be found now.

### What to build
Walk the finished, connected product once as a user would, record what is true, and link the evidence. **Find and file; do not fix.** A defect becomes a ticket (build-loop) and a row in the report; Innocent's sign-off (NL-133) is blocked on any open `blocking` finding.

**Setup.** The release-candidate stack from the committed Compose config, the NL-112 unit loaded, the seeded accounts (NL-82). Drive a real browser with the Chrome DevTools MCP (per the global browser rule) or Playwright if it is not connected; take a snapshot and a screenshot before the first click and after every state change.

**The walkthrough (Given/when/then per row, in `QA_REPORT.md`).** Journeys, each on the real backend:
1. Sign in as each role; wrong role refused (SCR-1).
2. Units list; upload the issued sheet and a bad file; validation report and choices (SCR-2…SCR-4).
3. Start a run from the prompt list; progress, pause, resume (SCR-5…SCR-7).
4. Unit board and the north-star tile (SCR-8).
5. Lesson workspace: edit, quote placeholder fill, standard decision, regenerate and adopt, history (SCR-9…SCR-12, SCR-16).
6. Submit, approve by the second account on the pinned version, send back, reopen (SCR-14, SCR-15).
7. Run summary (SCR-17).
Cut-order screens (SCR-13, SCR-18…SCR-21) are walked only if their ticket landed; otherwise the report says "cut #n, not built".

**For every walked screen:** every state in its SCR state matrix reached or marked "not reachable" with why; **axe** with 0 serious or critical findings at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark; a visual check against the D1 Clear Ledger look sheet and `docs/design/design.md`; copy frames the tool as expert-driven (GR-16).

**Lighthouse** (accessibility, best practices, performance) on SCR-8, SCR-9 and SCR-14, desktop and mobile. Targets [T]: accessibility ≥ 95, best practices ≥ 90; performance is recorded, not gated (the VPS is not production hosting, `capacity-and-workload.md`).

**TRACEABILITY.** `docs/ux/05-verify/TRACEABILITY.md` has one line per FE/INT ticket (UX-5a rows). Add a link column cell to each row pointing at its `QA_REPORT.md` section; a row with no evidence is listed as a finding. Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

### Sources
- `docs/ux/03-structure/SCREEN_SPECS.md` (state matrices, signed), `docs/ux/03-structure/IA.md`; `docs/design/design.md` and the D1 look sheet; `docs/ux/05-verify/TRACEABILITY.md` (rows added by NL-55…NL-60, NL-90…NL-101, NL-113…NL-115)
- Skill `ux-pipeline` UX-5 (a/b) in `.claude/skills/ux-pipeline/`; INTERFACE.md for the contract behaviour each screen shows
- PRD GR-16, R-58; `.claude/rules/` modern-ui and accessibility rules (WCAG 2.2)
- **Brief check:** serves "Thoughtful design and easy to understand/use/navigate workflow"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] every core screen was walked on the connected app and each state in its matrix is reached or justified — verify: `grep -cE '^### SCR-' docs/ux/05-verify/QA_REPORT.md` and the state tables inside — evidence: SCR-1…SCR-12 and SCR-14…SCR-17 each have a section with Given/when/then rows, a screenshot path and result `pass`, `finding-<id>` or `not reachable (why)` — covers: SCR-1, SCR-2, SCR-3, SCR-4, SCR-5, SCR-6, SCR-7, SCR-8, SCR-9, SCR-10, SCR-11, SCR-12, SCR-14, SCR-15, SCR-16, SCR-17
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] axe reports 0 serious or critical issues at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark, on every walked screen — verify: the axe run recorded per screen in the report (`npx @axe-core/cli` or the DevTools audit) — evidence: a table of screens × four modes, each 0 serious/critical, or a finding id — covers: GR-16
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] Lighthouse scores are recorded for SCR-8, SCR-9, SCR-14 (desktop and mobile) against accessibility ≥ 95 and best practices ≥ 90 — verify: `mcp__chrome-devtools__lighthouse_audit` or `npx lighthouse` output saved under `docs/ux/05-verify/lighthouse/` — evidence: six reports linked; each score printed; a miss is a finding, performance only recorded — covers: R-57
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] every UX-5a TRACEABILITY row has a link to its QA_REPORT section — verify: `awk -F'|' 'NR>2 && $NF ~ /^ *$/ {print}' docs/ux/05-verify/TRACEABILITY.md` — evidence: no row with an empty link cell, or each empty one is a finding — covers: SCR-8, SCR-9, SCR-14

(the )?writers' apps/web/app apps/web/src` — evidence: the text shows literally, no dialog; no copy match — covers: R-58, GR-16, CON-G6

## [NL-127] capacity: 200-user spike on the VPS (2-min ramp, 15-min plateau, provider stubbed) and load report

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — As a content lead judging whether to trust this tool, I need … the page-speed probe, and, if built, the editor load script …, so that every number in the demo has its *n* and a source. The brief asks that "loading/editing of lessons should be performant and be able to handle staff of 20+ reviewers"; Innocent set the bar at 500 users a day with a 200-user spike (PD-33), so this is the run that shows whether the stack holds it and says honestly where it does not.

### What to build
Run NL-118's load probe against the full Compose stack on the VPS and publish the result. **Run and report; do not tune.** A missed target is reported with the scale-path step that would fix it (`capacity-and-workload.md` *Scale path*), not fixed here.

**Pre-flight.** `df -h /home` shows enough free disk for logs and the database (the VPS disk is nearly full; stop and tell Innocent if under 3 GB free); `nproc` and `free -g` recorded for the report header; the stack is the committed Compose config with Postgres unpublished; the seeded unit from NL-112 is loaded so lessons are real size (~3,300 words); the **model provider is stubbed** (the worker's stub adapter, NL-79): no real model call is made, so spend is $0.

**The run.** `npm run load:spike` (NL-118): 200 virtual users in the DO capacity mix (70% reading/editing a lesson with a heartbeat every 15 s, 20% on polling screens at 1 poll / 2 s, 10% authors/approvers, page loads about every 30 s), a **2-minute ramp, a 15-minute plateau and a 2-minute ramp down** (`capacity-and-workload.md` *Workload assumptions*), with a generation run in flight on the stub so the worker and the polls compete as in real use. It writes a `probe_run` row (WF-29: p95s, error rate, connection counts, event-loop lag, *n*, machine, stub stated) and `evals/reports/load-<date>.md`. If NL-119 (the Yjs socket script, cut #1) landed, run `npm run load:spike -- --yjs` as well (WF-30: remote-edit p95, stored p95, lost updates, reconnect time, store transaction time); if it was cut, the report says "Yjs latency was not measured".

**Recovery.** After the plateau, keep sampling for 5 minutes and report the time until p95s return to the pre-spike level.

Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

### Sources
- `docs/design/capacity-and-workload.md` (decision, mix, burst shape, targets, recovery, scale path); DO-5 S14 (`eval-plan.md`); DO-6 WF-29, WF-30 (`observability.md`); DO-7 M-18…M-24, M-27
- NL-118 (probe), NL-119 (Yjs script, cut #1), NL-23 (Compose stack); CON-9, CON-11, CON-12, CON-20
- PRD PD-33, R-56, R-57, R-55; `.claude/rules/` build-loop notes on CPU contention (run nothing else during the plateau)
- **Brief check:** serves "loading/editing of lessons should be performant and be able to handle staff of 20+ reviewers"; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] a load run at 200 virtual users with a 2-minute ramp and a 15-minute plateau was executed on the VPS and its machine, stub and *n* are stated (WF-29) — verify: `ls evals/reports/load-*.md` and the report header — evidence: header with git SHA, prompt version (n/a, stubbed), model IDs (stub), `nproc`, RAM, 200 users, ramp and plateau times, requests counted — covers: R-57, EV-S14, EV-R1
- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] lesson open p95 < 1.5 s and unit board p95 < 1 s at the plateau (WF-29) — verify: report rows from the `probe_run` row — evidence: M-18 and M-20 printed with *n* and pass or missed — covers: R-57, M-18, M-20
- [ ] AC-3 [invariant] board and progress poll p95 < 300 ms, error rate < 0.5% and recovery ≤ 2 min (WF-29) — verify: report rows for M-21, M-22, M-23 — evidence: each value with *n* and pass or missed; a miss names the scale-path step — covers: M-21, M-22, M-23, EV-S14
- [ ] AC-4 [invariant] zero lost acknowledged updates, if the Yjs script landed, else the report says it was not measured (WF-30) — verify: `psql` on `probe_run` for the Yjs row or the report sentence — evidence: lost updates 0 with remote-edit p95 < 500 ms and stored p95 < 3 s (M-19, M-24, M-27), or the sentence "Yjs latency was not measured (cut #1)" — covers: R-56, M-19, M-24, M-27
- [ ] AC-5 [capture] the probe wrote its run record at its real entry point (WF-29) — verify: `psql -c "select id, users, p95_open_ms, error_rate from probe_run order by started_at desc limit 1"` — evidence: one `probe_run` row carrying the run configuration (users, machine, stub flag) and the p95s that the report prints — covers: OBS-6, OBS-1
- [ ] AC-6 [negative] no real model call was made and no key was needed — verify: `docker compose logs worker | grep -c 'api.anthropic.com'` and `select count(*) from model_call where created_at > '<run start>'` — evidence: 0 and 0 real-provider rows — covers: R-55, OBS-7
- [ ] AC-7 [invariant] a missed target is reported as missed with the scale-path step, nothing is tuned in this ticket — verify: report *Misses* section and `git diff --name-only` — evidence: each miss lists measured vs target and the step (2, 3 or 4); the diff has no source file — covers: R-57
- [ ] AC-8 [regression/context] dev-log entry with headline numbers; `.claude/state/resume.md` next action — verify: `git diff --name-only` — evidence: only `evals/reports/load-<date>.md`, the dev-log file and `.claude/state/resume.md`

### Evaluation

### Metrics

restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Platform work for the §9 experiment stage (GP-21, GP-44, GP-51): after the error-analysis round names the failure types (`FT-N`), experiment XP-1 changes exactly one thing aimed at one failure type and scores it on the frozen development set, with score and cost before and after. This is the first of up to three; XP-2 and XP-3 are slots.

### What to build
Run one experiment (`docs/testing/experiments/XP-1-<slug>.md`, zero-to-hero `ARTIFACT-MAP.md` §9). The target and the change are **chosen from the round-1 error analysis** (`docs/testing/error-analysis/<date>-round-1.md`, NL-120, reviewed by Innocent); this ticket's planner reads that file and fills the plan with them. Nothing here names a prompt change in advance: no tuning before the failure type is named.

- **Target:** one `FT-N` from the round-1 taxonomy. Prefer the failure type with the most traces whose fix lives in a prompt, schema, check or parameter (DO-5 *Failure categories*, "Fix lives in").
- **The one change:** a single variable in a single place: one prompt-layer edit (guidance or locked layer, via the prompt version path, never a UI edit of the locked layer: GR-18), or one model setting, or one check/schema tweak. Not two.
- **Frozen set:** the development cases `evals/cases/**` (S1–S3, S7, WP-1…WP-5, SYN), `docs/data/samples/**` and `docs/data/worked-pairs.md`. It is never edited to make a result pass; any expected-output change is a separate commit by rule (DO-5) and is out of scope here.
- **Scoring:** run `npm run eval:golden -- --suite drafts --repeat 3` (S3, real model, about $1.64 per run) and the golden tier (`--suite intake,checks`) **before** and **after** the change at otherwise identical settings; attach both reports and the cost (EV-R2). Spend is real model spend inside the PD-29 $75 ceiling (about $3.30 for the two S3 runs).
- **Decision:** keep if the target `FT-N` count falls on the frozen set with no new failure type appearing and no passing case flipping to failing; otherwise revert the change in a separate commit and record "reverted". Either outcome is a finished experiment.
- **Record fields** (one line each, greppable): `Target: FT-N`, `Change: <file> — <one-line diff summary>`, `Before:`, `After:`, `Cost:`, `Decision: keep|reverted`.
- Order: XP-1 starts after NL-120 merges.
- Must not: change two variables, edit the frozen set, use any text from `docs/source/restricted/` as an in-context example (GR-9, GR-11), or touch a file outside the one declared in `Change:` (plus the record and the two reports).

### Sources
- zero-to-hero `ARTIFACT-MAP.md` §9; DO-5 (*Failure categories*, *Baselines*, S3 acceptance, `EV-R2` change rule); round-1 file `docs/testing/error-analysis/` (NL-120); NL-109's S3 suite and report
- DO-6 WF-24, WF-25; DO-7 M-5, M-31; PRD R-51, GR-10, GR-11, GR-18

Delivery (no US) — `hiring-partner-framing` requires the demo to open with the business value, prove the brief's problem and close on the metric, and to speak only decisions that are in the record. Why now: the numbers exist (NL-112, NL-120), the script (NL-136) and the video (NL-138) must be written from the record, not from memory.

### What to build
Write the **decision inventory** and bring the framing document up to date with what was measured. Two files, one owner (this ticket).

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy

frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Delivery (R-23, cut #2) — the advisory judge may appear in a report only if it agrees with Innocent's labels (≥ 0.8 on ≥ 20, confirmed on the 10 held back). This ticket runs the calibration once and writes down the answer, whichever way it falls.

### What to build
Run NL-111's calibration script on Innocent's labels (NL-122) and publish the record.

1. **Pre-flight.** `evals/judge/labels.csv` has ≥ 28 labelled rows and `evals/judge/split.json` (20 calibration, 10 held back) was committed before the labels (NL-122 AC-2). `with-provider-env --check` names `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (NL-02). If it does not, or Innocent said "no judge", stop: the ticket closes as unused (cut #2) and the report is not written.
2. **Run** `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env --project-env .env -- npm run eval:judge-calibrate` (WF-31). It sends each pair (activity, standard text, rubric) to the judge on **OpenRouter** (a different provider from the generator, PD-12), compares each verdict with Innocent's label, and writes an `eval_run` and one `eval_case_result` per pair. Cost is cents; print it.
3. **Read the rule from DO-5 S12:** the judge enters any reported score only at **agreement ≥ 0.8 on ≥ 20 calibration labels, confirmed on the 10 held back**. The held-back 10 are scored once, last, and never used to edit the rubric. If agreement is below 0.8, the report says so and the judge stays off: the S9 report keeps no judge column, the docs say "the judge was built and did not meet its agreement bar" with the number. Do not edit the rubric against the held-back 10; a rubric change needs a new calibration round (new ticket, new split) and re-runs S12.
4. **Write `evals/reports/judge-calibration.md`:** agreement and *n* for the 20, the result on the 10 held back, the disagreements listed by `pair_id` (not the activity text beyond one line), judge model ID and prompt version, git SHA. Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

### Sources
- DO-5 S12 (`docs/design/eval-plan.md`: *Judges*, *Acceptance conditions*, *Development and held-out separation*); DO-6 WF-31; DO-7 M-34
- NL-111 (calibration script), NL-122 (labels), NL-110 (judge); CON-13; PRD R-23, PD-12, PD-17 / §6.4 (cut #2)

## [NL-134] evals: score the XPs on the frozen set; re-run the unit only if the prompt changed; final full-run report (`gate::paid`)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-36 — every number in the demo needs its *n* and a source. After the experiments (NL-128…130) each change has to be scored against the same frozen set as before, and the final full-run report has to describe the prompt that will actually be shown (GP-21, GP-51).

### What to build
Score what the experiments changed, decide with a rule whether the whole unit must run again, and publish the final report.

1. **Score each experiment.** For every `XP-N` that landed (NL-128, 129, 130; a slot closed unused is recorded as closed), run its recorded score command on the **frozen set** named in its record (WP-1…WP-5 golden cases and the stated development set) with the pre-change and post-change prompt versions: `npm run eval:golden -- --suite drafts --repeat 3` for model-driven cases (WF-24) and the targeted suite for its `FT-N`. Write `docs/testing/experiments/XP-N-result.md`: the `FT-N`, the one variable, score before / after with *n*, cost before / after, the decision (**kept**, **reverted**), and the commit. A change is kept only if its named `FT-N` improved and no other suite fell (golden tier 100% stays 100%).
2. **The rerun rule.** Compare `prompt_version` (and model, schema, check set) of the NL-112 run with the version that will be shipped. **Unchanged:** do not rerun; refresh the report with the XP scores and the sentence "the shipped prompt version equals the one in run <run_id>". **Changed:** rerun the whole unit exactly as NL-112 (`npm run eval:full-run -- --unit G6-U4`, same settings; one run), after the headroom check against the PD-29 $75 ceiling (stop and ask Innocent if it does not fit, `gate::paid`). Never rerun to chase a better number with the same version.
3. **Final report.** `evals/reports/full-run-<run_id>.md` is the report the docs and video quote; the older one stays in the repo, linked as superseded. Reconcile the totals the same way as NL-112 (OBS-8). Update the S9 line in `docs/design/eval-plan.md` *Baselines* only through a dev-log-explained commit (the table says "none yet" until a run sets it).
4. Print total build spend against the $75 ceiling (M-29).

Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

## [NL-135] evals: seeded-error report ("our reviewers")

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
US-34 — As a content lead (P-3), I need … the seeded-error catch rate, each with its *n*, so that I can judge the drafts and the review, not just the speed. This ticket scores NL-124's blind review against the planter's key and reports it with the honest label: our reviewers, one reviewer, about 5 errors.

### What to build
After NL-124's "seeded review done", unseal the key and score it.

1. `npm run eval:seed -- --score <eval_run_id>` (NL-92) matches each planted error in `evals/local/seed-key.json` to what happened: **caught by a check** (an `issue` before any human), **caught by the reviewer**, **caught at approval**, or **missed (approved with the error)**. Caught-before-approval = the first three.
2. Write `evals/reports/seeded-<run_id>.md`: planted count, caught count by route, missed list by error kind (not the lesson text), catch rate = caught before approval ÷ planted, with *n* and the label **"our reviewers: one reviewer (Innocent), n = k planted"**. Compare with the S10 bar: ≥ 90% caught (aspiration), < 70% fails the guard; with about 5 errors, 5 of 5 meets the aspiration, 4 of 5 is reported as is, 3 or fewer fails; the **wrong-code plant must be caught (floor)**.
3. Say what the number does and does not show: one reviewer, a tiny *n*, planted errors are not the full range of real ones. Never write that Newsela's reviewers catch anything. A miss is reported, with what it means for the north star (M-1 is then not to be read as a saving, G-3).
4. Seal again: the key stays git-ignored; the report names kinds, not locations. Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

- [ ] AC-2 [invariant] the catch rate is judged against the S10 bar and the wrong-code plant is reported separately as the floor (WF-26) — verify: report rows for M-4 and the wrong-code plant — evidence: rate with pass, reported-as-is, or fail wording as per the bar; wrong-code plant caught yes/no — covers: M-4, EV-S10
- [ ] AC-3 [capture] every planted error has a result row and the scoring ran at the real entry point (WF-26) — verify: `psql -c "select count(*), count(distinct case_id) from eval_case_result where eval_run_id = '<id>'"` — evidence: one row per planted error; counts match the report; the planter and reviewer user ids differ — covers: OBS-6, EV-R1

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy

restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or

### Story
Delivery (no US) — the demo and the interview are where this build is judged. `hiring-partner-framing` sets the order: open with the business value in the partner's words, prove the brief's problem, close on the metric; and tell every decision in the interview shape (choice, rejected alternative, evidence, limit).

### What to build
Write two documents from the inventory (NL-131), the measured reports and the walkthrough (NL-126). Nothing is narrated from memory.

**1. `docs/delivery/<YYYY-MM-DD>-demo-script.md`.** Table: `time · on screen · narration · source row (inventory id) · evidence path`. Order: (a) the problem in Newsela's words ("ARR … 10's of millions", "prohibitively enormous manual authoring work"); (b) what success means, in both layers, and the north star with its guard (M-1 with G-2; seeded-error M-4); (c) the flow narrated by the thing the partner cares about: upload → outline defects caught before any money is spent → generation (the unit plan, one call per lesson) → **a lesson picked at random** (GR-14) → a blocked Approve (grounding placeholder or standards confirmation) → the second account approves the pinned version → the success surface; (d) **one caught error shown** (GR-14); (e) decisions, cuts and candour: the limits section (one reviewer, n = k; Compose not hosted; what was cut). **Product under 5 minutes first, then up to 5 minutes of decisions** (total ≤ 10; the brief sets no length), each decision cites an inventory row marked `decided`. Every number shown or spoken carries its *n* and a path (NL-112/NL-134 reports, NL-123, NL-127, NL-135 if built). Add a shot list line per row for the `demo-video` skill, and a "cannot be shown" list (cut items) so the video never implies them.

**2. `docs/delivery/<YYYY-MM-DD>-interview-prep.md`.** One table, two layers: question a reviewer would ask · the business-value answer (layer 2, one sentence) · the technical answer (layer 1: **choice, rejected alternative, evidence with path and *n*, limit**). At least the top ten inventory rows, plus: why one call per lesson (SP-1), why the freeze at Submit (SP-2), how grounding works and what it cannot catch (SP-3), the north-star metric and how it could mislead, what the judge/held-out comparison show or why they were cut, capacity (PD-33) and how we know, what we would do with another week. Follow the interview-feedback guidance in `.claude/rules/hiring-partner-framing.md` (*Interview-preparation route*): spend most of an answer on Innocent's architecture, decision, rejected alternative, verification and limit.

Rule: the tool is framed as expert-driven (GR-16); never "replaces writers". Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

## [NL-137] release: pre-deploy full suite, clean Compose up from the committed config, start events present, one `pg_dump` (PD-30)

_Conventions for every Newsela Lesson Studio issue:_ repo `innocentnortey/inno-newsela` (VPS working copy
`/home/linuxuser/workspaces/inno-newsela`); read `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/README.md`, `.claude/reference/area-map.md`
and `docs/plans/HANDOFF-PHASE-B.md` first; vocabulary from `docs/design/component-contracts.md` (DO-4) and
`docs/contracts/INTERFACE.md`. Build-loop tickets go plan → implement → test → review (`.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md`;
frozen tests first only for `risk::security`); only affected tests run. Never: quote or read `docs/source/restricted/`
into code, prompts, fixtures or issues (GR-9); copy a provider key (use `/home/linuxuser/workspaces/bin/with-provider-env`);
restate or contradict an agreed `CON-N` (changes go through `docs/contracts/CHANGES.md` as `CHG-N`); use real student or
staff data (synthetic, seeded, traceable). Evidence is a command and its output, attached to the issue.

### Story
Delivery (no US) — GR-14 and the "nothing deploys on a red full suite" rule (`build-loop-test-scope.md`) meet here. The video (NL-138) and the submission (NL-143) must describe a build that was proven from a clean checkout, with every process recording its start and one backup taken after the last run (PD-30).

### What to build
Prove the release candidate and tag it. **Check and report; do not fix.** If anything fails, file a build-loop ticket and stop: this ticket changes no source, configuration, test or lockfile.

**Lane flag for the orchestrator.** The plan keeps this ticket `lane::direct`: it runs commands, takes a backup file and commits a Markdown record. If a check forces a change to config that code reads (Compose file, `render.yaml`, settings defaults, scripts), that change is a separate `lane::build-loop` ticket and this one resumes after it merges; do not edit it here.

Steps, in order, each stopping at the first red (`build-loop-test-scope.md`: cheapest first):
1. **Clean tree on `main`.** `git status --porcelain` empty; no unpushed commit: `git log origin/main..main` empty.
2. **Full suite (EV-R3).** `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (all projects, not affected-only), `npm run eval:golden -- --suite intake,checks` (no model calls), `npm run test:e2e`. Record counts and wall time.
3. **Clean Compose up from the committed config.** `git clone . /tmp/nl137 && cd /tmp/nl137 && docker compose config -q && docker compose -p nl137 up -d --build`, wait for healthy, then run the migrations and seed (`npm run db:migrate`, `npm run db:seed` through the documented route). Tear down at the end with `down -v` (never touch other projects' containers).
4. **Start events (WF-38).** Each process (web, worker, collaboration server) wrote one `ops_event` start row with a non-empty `build_id` (the local git SHA, or `RENDER_GIT_COMMIT` on Render).
5. **Network exposure (OBS-10).** Postgres is not published outside the Compose network: `docker compose -p nl137 ps` shows no host port for it, and a connection to the host's 5432 from outside the network is refused.
6. **One backup (WF-40, PD-30).** On the real stack that holds the final full-run data (not the throwaway clone): `npm run ops:backup`; check the `ops_event` row (dump path, size, SHA-256) and `pg_restore --list` reads the dump. The dump file is git-ignored and stays on the VPS.
7. **Repository facts.** `LICENSE` exists at the root (GR-17: all rights reserved, evaluation use permitted); `render.yaml` is committed and no Render service was provisioned for it (PD-15 option D); no file under `docs/source/restricted/` is tracked (`git ls-files docs/source/restricted | wc -l` = 0).
8. **Tag.** `git tag release-<short-sha>` and push `origin main --tags` only (factory mode, PD-34). Write `docs/delivery/<YYYY-MM-DD>-release-check.md` with the SHA, command outputs (counts, not logs) and the backup row. Lane guard (`ticket-lanes`): before committing, `git diff --name-only` must list no file that code or tests read (source, tests, schemas, migrations, prompts, settings, lockfiles, fixtures, CI); if it does, stop, relabel the ticket `lane::build-loop` and report. Commit straight to `main` (factory mode, PD-34).

### Sources
- `.claude/rules/build-loop-test-scope.md` (full suite before every deploy; nothing deploys on red); `.claude/rules/gauntlet-hosting-default.md`; PRD PD-15 (option D), PD-30 (backup), GR-17
- DO-6 WF-38, WF-40 (`docs/design/observability.md`); NL-23 (Compose, `render.yaml`), NL-83 (`ops:backup`)
- DO-5 `eval-plan.md` *Verification and evidence* (EV-R3)
- **Brief check:** serves "Source Code" with "Clean, well structured architecture" and a runnable build; touches nothing out of scope; weakens nothing → proceed.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-1 [invariant] the tree is clean and the full suite is green on the release SHA (EV-R3) — verify: `git status --porcelain; npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run eval:golden -- --suite intake,checks && npm run test:e2e` — evidence: empty status; all commands exit 0 with counts recorded in the release check; a red stops the ticket — covers: EV-R3
